The Wisdom of David Bowie: On Art, Religion, Technology and More
items.summary: It doesn’t quite ring true to call David Bowie a rock star. Ziggy Stardust, the neon synthetic-clad alien alter ego he both created and retired in the early seventies, was, of course, rock stardom outlandishly personified. then, that was the concept of what turned out to be just one of many personae he deliberately crafted throughout the course of his career. That career was in music, primarily, but looking back on it today, more than a decade after Bowie’s death, it looks more like his medium was culture itself. That’s underscored by his interviews, clips from a variety of which appear in the new video above from YouTube channel T&H Inspiration. Most of T&H’s most popular videos add visuals to speeches by the popularizer of Eastern philosophy Alan Watts, who’s been featured here on Open Culture before. He and Bowie had more in common than it may seem at first, beginning with an Englishness that remained thoroughgoing no matter how far out they ventured into the world. Though Watts’ interest in Buddhism hardly needs stating, it’s worth remembering that he chose to be ordained as an Episcopalian priest rather than as a Buddhist monk. The young Bowie, for his part, very nearly took the latter path, studying under the late Lama Chime Rinpoche, who eventually told him he’d be better off going into the music business. Bowie did so, of course, but with a new “sense of transience and change, which actually became fundamental to my life and my approach to it,” as he put it decades later. That sense manifests even in his early work, but embracing and even pursuing impermanence — the impermanence of sounds, of fashions, of hit records, of life itself — also kept him from getting mired in the irrelevance or auto-kitsch that threatens every superstar. Given the belief that nothing lasts forever, “looking for the source of one’s own being becomes much more important,” as does attempting artistic or intellectual challenges at the very edge of one’s abilities. Alan Watts would probably have agreed. The bigger question is, did he ever hear “Changes”?

items.title: 別當冤大頭｜大禹嶺、福壽山、梨山到底差在哪？2026台灣頂級高山茶選購指南：產地直送的真心話
items.summary: 一次比較產區、海拔、香氣、口感、價格與適合族群，並整理2026高山茶真假辨識、溯源QR Code及產地直送避坑方法。想買台灣頂級高山茶，卻被「大禹嶺、福壽山、梨山」搞得一頭霧水？同樣標示青心烏龍、同樣來自高海拔，有的半斤一千多元，有的卻要三、四千元；網路上更常出現「高冷茶」「私房茶園」「產地直送」等說法，讓人越看越難選。先說結論：大禹嶺、福壽山與梨山不是三種茶樹品種，而是不同產區或市場慣用的產地名稱。三者多以青心烏龍製作成輕發酵、半球形的高山烏龍，真正拉開差距的，是茶園位置、海拔與微氣候、季節、採製技術、保存方式，以及來源是否可信。如果你只想快速選：追求細緻、清甜與稀有感，可看大禹嶺；偏好厚實茶湯、果香與均衡層次，可選福壽山；想要高山香氣明顯、選擇多且預算較好掌握，梨山通常最實際。梨山茶：範圍最廣，也是多數人的高山茶入門首選梨山茶不是單一山頭或單一茶園，而是一個較廣義的產區概念。農業部茶及飲料作物改良場指出，梨山茶區因海拔高、氣溫低，部分區段一年僅採收二至三次；茶菁較肥厚，成茶常呈翠綠色，茶湯蜜綠帶黃，特色是香氣清揚、滋味清醇鮮爽。因範圍大，梨山茶可從香氣奔放、容易入口的日常款，一路找到冷冽細緻、接近頂級山頭表現的高階款。這也是為什麼同樣寫著「梨山茶」，價格可能差上一倍以上。選梨山茶時，別只看包裝正面的四個字，還要問清楚：茶園位於哪個區域、哪一季採收、品種為何、是手採或機採、發酵與焙火程度，以及是否有溯源資訊。若賣家只反覆強調「高山」「雲霧」「老師傅」，卻不願交代基本資料，建議先不要買大份量。第一次接觸高山茶、希望兼顧香氣與性價比，或想買一款全家都容易接受的茶。福壽山茶：茶湯厚、甜感飽滿，送禮辨識度高福壽山位於梨山地區，市場上通常把福壽山茶獨立列為更精細的山頭類別。它與廣義梨山茶並非完全對立，而比較像「產區」與「特定名區」的關係。許多茶友喜歡福壽山茶，是因為它常呈現較飽滿的花果香、厚實滑順的茶湯，以及清楚而持久的回甘。沖泡得宜時，香氣不只停留在杯口，茶湯本身也會有甜潤感；這種「香與水有連結」的表現，通常比只有高香、入口卻薄的茶更耐喝。「福壽山」三個字也有品牌溢價。真正值得付高價的，應是來源清楚、採製完整、茶湯乾淨且數泡後仍有甜度的茶，而不是只有華麗禮盒與模糊的高海拔敘述。喜歡濃郁花果香、重視茶湯厚度，或需要有產區知名度的送禮茶。大禹嶺茶：量少價高，最需要冷靜查證大禹嶺常被視為台灣高山茶的頂端產區之一。高海拔、低溫、日照較短，使茶芽生長較慢，市場上的優質大禹嶺茶常被描述為葉質厚、果膠感明顯、口感柔滑，並帶有清冷花香、果香與悠長回甘。但大禹嶺也是最容易讓消費者「為名字買單」的類別。真正高海拔茶園面積有限，加上環境與土地使用條件，市場供應不可能無限。若商品長年大量現貨、價格卻只比一般梨山茶略高，或只用「XXK」公路里程當作唯一證明，都應提高警覺。2026年市面實際商品可見大禹嶺茶以75克小包販售，單價換算後明顯高於一般梨山茶；零售價格仍會受到採收季節、茶園、等級、通路及包裝影響，不能只靠「越貴越真」判斷。已喝過多款高山茶、能辨識茶湯細緻度，且願意為稀有產地與乾淨尾韻付費的人。2026高山茶價格怎麼看？台灣茶常用「一斤600克、半斤300克、四兩150克、二兩75克」計價。網購時若沒先換算重量，很容易被低總價誤導。以下是選購時可參考的一般市場觀察區間，不是官方定價，也不是判定真假的標準：若價格明顯低於區間，不代表一定是假茶，也可能是較低海拔原料、混批、非當季、碎茶或直接讓利；相反地，高價也不等於高品質，先試喝75克或150克，比直接買一斤更安全。春茶受冬季休眠與春季回暖影響，常見茶湯厚、滋味完整、耐泡度佳；冬茶在冷涼氣候下製作，常呈現清揚香氣與細緻口感。但每年天候不同，採收時間、降雨、日照和製茶師判斷，都可能改變成品。喜歡清香、冷冽感與輕盈尾韻：可優先試冬茶。想追求性價比：不要只買季節名氣，直接比較同店家兩季的小包茶樣。「產地直送」真的比較可靠嗎？產地直送只表示銷售路徑的宣稱，並不自動證明茶葉就來自該產區。茶農自售可能減少通路加價，也更容易問到採收與製作細節；但如果沒有清楚標示與可查資料，「茶農直送」四個字仍可能只是行銷用語。農糧署表示，自2023年起，當年度生產且以完整包裝流通、標示為國產的茶葉，應依規定標示溯源農糧產品追溯條碼、產銷履歷或有機標章等可追溯資訊。2026年修正的追溯條碼管理規範也明定，業者使用的條碼應與系統登錄產品資訊相符，且不得轉借他人。收到茶葉後建議立刻掃描QR Code，核對生產者、產品及產地資訊是否與包裝和賣場頁面一致。有QR Code是基本加分，但不是風味保證；拒當冤大頭：買高山茶前必查7件事1.看清楚重量與單位價格把所有商品換算成每75克或每300克再比價。低價小包不一定便宜，大盒裝也不代表划算。2.問具體產區，不只問海拔海拔數字可以寫得很漂亮，但產區、季節與茶園批次更有辨識價值。若對方只說「兩千多公尺」卻不說大致位置，資訊仍不完整。3.核對溯源QR Code掃碼後應能連到正式的追溯資訊，內容須與商品相符。不要只看包裝上有一個QR Code圖樣就放心。4.查看產地與原產地標示「台灣製造」「台灣包裝」不等於茶菁產自台灣。購買國產高山茶時，應確認原料產地，而不是只看公司地址。5.先買小包，再追同批次初次購買建議從75克或150克開始。喝到喜歡的批次，再詢問是否能追加同季、同批茶，風險遠低於第一次就買一斤。6.不迷信顆粒越綠、香氣越衝越好開袋香氣強，也可能只是焙火、保存或製程造成。更應觀察茶湯是否乾淨、入口有厚度、吞嚥後是否回甘，以及連泡數次後會不會迅速變薄。7.保留包裝、訂單與賣場說明高單價茶若發現產地或標示疑慮，完整的商品頁截圖、發票、外包裝與未沖泡茶樣，都是後續詢問或申訴的重要資料。頂級高山茶不需要用滾水猛泡很久，但水溫太低也難以展開茶葉。茶水比：每100毫升水使用約5～7克茶葉。第一泡：浸泡約40～60秒，再依茶壺大小與個人口味調整。茶具：瓷壺或蓋碗最容易客觀呈現香氣與缺點，初次試茶尤其合適。好茶的重點不是「可以泡十幾次」的宣傳數字，而是每一泡是否仍有香、甜、厚度與乾淨感。最貴的不一定最適合，資訊透明才是真正的頂級大禹嶺勝在稀有與細緻，福壽山常有飽滿厚甜的層次，梨山則有更寬廣的選擇與相對友善的預算。真正懂買的人，不會只追最高海拔或最響亮的山頭，而是看產區資訊、採收季節、溯源標示、試喝表現與價格是否合理。先喝懂自己的偏好，再為產區升級，才能把每一分預算花在茶湯裡，而不是花在名稱與包裝上。產區與海拔只是品質條件之一，茶園管理、採摘成熟度、發酵、揉捻、乾燥與保存都會影響結果。主要原因包括高海拔環境、產量有限、採收與運輸成本較高，以及市場需求與品牌溢價。但價格高不是產地真實或品質優良的充分證明，仍要查溯源與實際試喝。確認原料產地標示，掃描國產茶溯源QR Code，核對生產者與產品資訊，並選擇能說明產區、季節、品種和批次的賣家。對價格異常低、來源含糊或宣稱大量稀有茶的商品保持警覺。高海拔通常帶來低溫、較慢生長與特定香氣條件，但若茶園管理或製茶不佳，仍不會自動成為好茶。 請參閱所附表格 ↛

items.title: 避雷攻略｜Dcard、PTT熱議10款高CP值咖啡豆推薦，小資族告別超商苦味
items.summary: 其實不用花上百元跑精品咖啡廳，只要選對咖啡豆，在宿舍、租屋處或辦公室也能用每杯約15～35元的成本，喝到帶有堅果、焦糖、巧克力甚至花果香氣的咖啡。但平價咖啡豆真的不是「越大包越划算」。Dcard與PTT咖啡板上，最常見的踩雷經驗包括：買到放太久的油耗豆、只看產區卻忽略烘焙度、怕酸卻誤買淺焙豆，以及一次囤了一公斤，最後喝不完只能放到走味。本篇整理10款適合學生、小資族與咖啡新手的高CP值咖啡豆，從清爽手沖、每日美式到濃郁拿鐵都有涵蓋，並教你看懂烘焙日期、風味標示與每杯成本，避開「便宜但難喝」的地雷。高CP值咖啡豆推薦！整理Dcard、PTT熱議10款咖啡豆1.貝仕特咖啡：小資族日常飲用的高CP值選擇想擺脫超商咖啡單調的焦苦味，又不想讓每天的咖啡預算失控，可以將貝仕特咖啡列入日常咖啡豆清單。整體風味以容易入口、平衡順口為主要方向，適合剛開始接觸咖啡豆的學生、小資族，以及每天都有喝咖啡習慣的人。偏好低酸風味，可優先挑選帶有堅果、可可、焦糖或奶油甜香的中焙至中深焙豆款；喜歡清爽黑咖啡，則可以選擇具有柑橘、茶香或柔和果甜感的中淺焙咖啡豆。無論使用手沖濾杯、美式咖啡機、摩卡壺或全自動咖啡機，都能依照個人習慣找到合適選擇。-風味平衡，適合作為每天飲用的咖啡豆可依黑咖啡、拿鐵等不同喝法挑選豆款對咖啡新手與怕酸族相對友善兼顧價格、香氣與日常飲用需求適合學生、小資族及辦公室族群適合口味：喜歡堅果、可可、焦糖甜香，以及不過度酸苦的咖啡風味。避雷提醒：購買前應先確認咖啡豆的烘焙度、風味描述及建議沖煮方式。怕酸者建議選中焙至中深焙；經常製作拿鐵，可選擇醇厚度較高的配方豆；喜歡手沖黑咖啡，則可嘗試香氣較明亮的中淺焙豆款。2.步昂咖啡豆：小預算入門花果香的首選步昂咖啡在PTT咖啡板具有一定討論度，除了不定期推出試喝或入門優惠，也經常提供耶加雪菲、肯亞及中南美洲單品豆。過去曾出現半磅三包的組合優惠，對想用有限預算探索不同產區的人相當友善。如果你第一次從超商咖啡轉向自己沖煮，可以先選品牌的中焙或中淺焙入門款，不必一開始就挑價格最高、風味最特殊的競標豆。-選擇多，容易找到平價入門豆常有組合包或新客優惠小包裝較不容易因喝不完而走味適合比較不同產區的香氣差異適合口味：喜歡柑橘、花香、莓果與茶感的人。避雷提醒：極淺焙豆對磨豆機與沖煮技術要求較高。新手若磨得太粗或水溫太低，可能只喝到尖銳酸味，建議先選中淺焙或中焙。3. Lavazza Qualità Oro金牌咖啡豆：進口大廠豆裡的安全牌Lavazza Qualità Oro又稱Lavazza金牌，採100%阿拉比卡豆，常見規格有250g、500g與1kg。PTT曾有使用者形容它香氣明顯、甜感佳且苦味雜味較少，也有人認為以手沖飲用時酸感稍高，但整體仍屬順口的安全牌。它的最大優點是通路多、價格容易掌握，不需要等烘豆店寄送。搭配摩卡壺、全自動咖啡機或美式咖啡機，都能得到相對穩定的表現。100%阿拉比卡，苦澀感通常比重焙羅布斯塔配方柔和適合口味：喜歡蜂蜜、堅果及柔和果香，又不想喝得太苦的人。避雷提醒：進口豆的包裝日期不等於烘焙日期。購買前要看有效期限、進口資訊與包裝完整度，開封後最好於一個月內飲用。4. Kirkland有機衣索比亞咖啡豆：想用大包裝喝到花果香可考慮好市多大包裝咖啡豆在PTT長期具有討論度，其中Kirkland有機衣索比亞豆常被拿來與其他深焙商業豆比較。衣索比亞咖啡通常具有花香、果香或莓果調性，相較傳統深焙豆，更容易讓剛接觸精品咖啡的人感受到「咖啡原來不只有苦味」。風味比一般深焙量販豆明亮適合每日喝兩杯以上或多人共飲黑咖啡與手沖都能使用適合口味：想從焦苦咖啡轉向花香、果香的人。避雷提醒：907g對單人飲用仍然偏多。如果每天只喝一杯，建議與朋友分購，或開封後立刻分成數個小包密封冷凍。5. Magnum熱帶雨林有機咖啡豆：怕酸族的大容量選擇Magnum熱帶雨林有機咖啡豆也是量販通路中常被討論的大包裝產品。整體走向通常偏堅果、可可與烘烤香氣，比花果型淺焙豆更容易被怕酸的人接受。它不一定具有精品單品豆的細緻層次，但作為每日美式、辦公室咖啡或拿鐵基底，風味直接、成本低，是相對實用的選擇。適合口味：喜歡堅果、烤吐司、可可與低酸咖啡的人。避雷提醒：若豆子表面大量出油，研磨後容易黏附在全自動咖啡機內。使用前先確認機器是否適合油脂較多的深焙豆。6. Peet’s Major Dickason’s Blend：濃郁拿鐵與冰咖啡首選喜歡咖啡味濃、加牛奶後仍然有存在感的人，可以考慮Peet’s Major Dickason’s Blend。這款屬於偏深焙、醇厚型配方，常見黑巧克力、焦糖、香料與微煙燻感。PTT的好市多咖啡豆討論中，也曾有使用者提到這款沖拿鐵表現不錯。若你的主要需求是奶咖，它通常比清淡的淺焙單品更合適。-醇厚度高，加奶不會被稀釋到沒有味道適合製作冰拿鐵及冰美式深焙風格明確，不用複雜沖法適合口味：喜歡黑巧克力、焦糖及重口味咖啡的人。避雷提醒：不建議用接近沸騰的水長時間萃取，否則焦苦味容易被放大。手沖可從85～88°C開始調整。7. cama經典配方豆：想複製連鎖咖啡風味的穩定選擇如果平常習慣喝cama，又希望降低每天外帶咖啡的費用，直接選擇品牌的經典配方豆，是最容易上手的方式之一。配方豆的目的不是展現單一產區，而是追求每一批風味穩定。常見調性包括焦糖、堅果、可可與柔和果香，無論使用義式咖啡機、美式咖啡機或濾杯，都相對容易入口。-實體店與官方通路容易購買不必花時間研究莊園及處理法適合口味：喜歡平衡、順口、不過酸也不過苦的咖啡。避雷提醒：品牌可能同時販售多種配方及單品豆，購買前要確認烘焙度。別只看包裝名稱就直接下單。8.路易莎經典配方豆：新手容易取得的入門豆路易莎門市密度高，臨時缺豆時相當方便。其配方豆多以大眾接受度為主，常見堅果、焦糖、奶油及可可風味，適合從超商咖啡轉向在家沖煮的初學者。如果你不知道自己喜歡哪種豆子，可以先在門市喝一杯對應咖啡，確認口味後再買整包，比盲買更不容易踩雷。可先喝成品再決定是否買豆適合租屋族與剛買咖啡機的人避雷提醒：門市現場剩餘的豆子不一定都是近期烘焙，結帳前仍要查看包裝日期與保存狀態。9. HWC黑沃義式配方豆：奶咖控的高CP值日常豆黑沃的義式配方多以巧克力、焦糖、堅果與厚實甜感為主，定位明確，適合義式咖啡機、摩卡壺或全自動咖啡機。對每天早上都喝拿鐵的人而言，與其買昂貴的花果型淺焙豆，再讓牛奶蓋掉大部分細緻香氣，不如選一款醇厚、穩定的中深焙配方豆，實際CP值反而更高。適合義式機與全自動咖啡機真正的問題通常是水溫太高、研磨太細或萃取時間過長；先調整參數，不必急著怪豆子。10.夏野豆行平價單品豆：想認識產區風味的小資選項Dcard咖啡相關討論中，曾有網友在詢問網路咖啡豆商家時推薦夏野豆行。這類在地網路烘豆店的優點，是通常能買到較新鮮的半磅包裝，也能選擇不同產區、處理法及烘焙度。新手可以先從衣索比亞水洗、巴西日曬或瓜地馬拉中焙開始，三者的香氣差異較容易辨認。避雷提醒：網友推薦具有個人口味差異，下單前仍應查看近期評價、出貨方式、烘焙日期及退換貨規則。假設購買一包300元、重量227g的咖啡豆，每杯使用15g：每杯咖啡豆成本約20元即使加上濾紙與飲用水，每杯通常仍可控制在25元左右若使用大包裝豆，每杯豆子成本甚至可能降至10～18元。前提是必須在風味明顯衰退前喝完。為了便宜而買太多，最後丟掉半包，反而完全沒有省到。咖啡豆避雷攻略：買之前一定要看這5點1.看烘焙日期，不只看有效期限有效期限只能表示食品在正常保存下的安全期限，不代表風味最佳期。咖啡豆購買時應優先尋找烘焙日期；如果只標示有效期限，至少要選擇包裝完整、距到期日較遠的商品。2.單人喝不要輕易買一公斤若每天使用15g，一公斤約可沖66杯。一天一杯要兩個多月才能喝完，後半包很可能已經失去香氣。除非多人共飲，否則227～500g通常更合理。3.怕酸別直接買極淺焙耶加雪菲「耶加雪菲」是產區名稱，不代表每一款都甜美無酸。怕酸的人可優先選巴西、中南美洲配方、中焙或中深焙豆，風味通常更接近堅果、可可與焦糖。4.奶咖與手沖應該選不同方向花香細緻的淺焙豆，加進大量牛奶後可能失去特色；手沖黑咖啡則可以嘗試水洗衣索比亞、肯亞或中淺焙單品。5.小心來路不明的高價莊園名稱購買高價藝伎或知名莊園豆時，要查看完整產區、莊園、批次與處理法資訊。2025年台灣曾發生知名咖啡品牌因莊園名稱標示爭議遭移送偵辦的事件，因此「包裝名稱很高級」並不足以證明豆子來源。-粉水比：1：15～1：16總時間：約2分～2分30秒水溫：89～92°C中焙豆兼具甜感與厚度，是新手最容易掌握的烘焙度。淺焙豆密度高，若使用過低水溫或磨得太粗，容易出現只有酸味、甜感不足的情況。咖啡豆保存方法：大包裝也能減少走味買回大包裝後，建議依一至兩週用量分裝。短期飲用的豆子放在避光、陰涼且乾燥的位置；一個月內喝不完的部分，可使用密封袋分裝後冷凍。最好每次只拿一份，直接研磨沖煮，避免水氣進入包裝。咖啡豆也不要放在冰箱冷藏室，因為冷藏室濕度高、氣味複雜，反而可能吸附異味。Q1：咖啡豆開封後可以放多久？若以風味為考量，建議開封後約四週內喝完。保存良好不代表超過四週就不能喝，而是花香、果香與甜感通常會逐漸下降。Q2：咖啡豆表面出油就是壞掉嗎？深焙豆因細胞結構較疏鬆，油脂較容易浮到表面。但若同時出現陳舊油味、蠟味或令人不舒服的氣味，就可能已經氧化。Q3：怕酸的人應該選哪種咖啡豆？可優先選巴西豆、中深焙配方豆，或標示堅果、巧克力、焦糖風味的產品。避免一開始就買極淺焙、柑橘酸值強烈的豆款。Q4：沒有義式咖啡機也能自己煮咖啡嗎？最省預算的方式是濾杯加濾紙；喜歡濃郁口感則可使用摩卡壺、法壓壺或愛樂壓。真正影響風味的關鍵，往往是磨豆機與新鮮研磨，而不是器材價格。Q5：買咖啡豆還是咖啡粉比較好？有磨豆機就選整豆，香氣保存通常較佳。若沒有磨豆機，可以請店家依器材研磨，但建議購買小包裝並盡快喝完。命定咖啡豆不一定最貴，而是最適合你的喝法學生與小資族挑咖啡豆，不需要一開始就追求昂貴藝伎或高分競標豆。真正的高CP值，是你能在新鮮期內喝完、沖煮方式不複雜，而且每天都願意再喝一杯。怕酸的人，可從巴西中焙、巧克力型配方或Magnum、Peet’s等濃郁豆款開始；喜歡清爽花果香，可嘗試步昂、夏野豆行或在地烘豆店的衣索比亞水洗豆；每天固定喝拿鐵，則適合cama、路易莎或黑沃的義式配方。別再只用「苦不苦」判斷咖啡好不好喝。當你第一次在咖啡裡喝到堅果甜香、焦糖餘韻或淡淡花香，或許就會明白：擺脫超商死苦味，不一定要提高預算，只需要選對豆子。

items.title: 從山神、鹿群到雲豹：陳芯宜走了20年，抵達《雲在兩千米》
items.summary: 導演陳芯宜在最新VR作品《雲在兩千米》中改編吳明益的短篇小說，帶領觀眾與主角一同在經歷喪妻打擊之後，透過追溯愛妻寫下的文字作品探索人心祕密，深入台灣山林追尋雲豹的足跡。每位觀眾配戴著頭戴式顯示器（簡稱頭顯），在6×7米的有限展演空間裡，潛入雲霧繚繞的台灣山林，探索虛實之間和生死之間的無垠世界。陳芯宜2022年以台灣白色恐怖歷史題材的VR作品《無法離開的人》，榮獲威尼斯影展「最佳沉浸體驗大獎」，2025年再度以VR新作《雲在兩千米》榮獲同一大獎，成為影史以連續兩部作品包辦全球VR最高榮譽第一人。曾在大自然中深刻體認到人類的渺小，她在創作中透過VR技術呈現多層次的宇宙，模糊了生死之間的界線，不僅撫慰了觀眾的傷逝之情，也撫慰了她自己。2026年，是陳芯宜忙碌多產的一年，她不僅推出了個人第三部VR《雲在兩千米》，並且拍攝完成了劇情長片《樹人》，將於明年（2027）推出。她在這兩部作品中分別以不同的形式，深入雲霧繚繞的台灣山林。這趟旅程的起點，其實要從20年前開始說起。2006年夏天，陳芯宜為了拍攝劇情長片《流浪神狗人》，與一同寫劇本的樓一安導演去東部，一邊田調勘景，一邊討論劇本，每天翻看地圖討論隔天要去哪裡。有天她在地圖看到花蓮秀林鄉銅門的清水溪（今名「慕谷慕魚」），一種奇異的直覺告訴她要去這裡，感覺就像那個地名在地圖上發著光呼喚著她。隔天他們辦好入山證入山已近傍晚4、5點，山中有只有他們兩人，溪谷中遍布巨石，美得宛如仙境。然而就在一瞬之間，所有鳥叫蟲鳴忽然靜止，接著溪水聲音如巨浪般襲來。她回憶：「就在那個瞬間，我忽然心生一種恐懼，但並不是山洪暴發之類的危險，而是覺得有『靈』要過來了，不能擋在這裡，必須馬上避開，從溪谷往岸上去。後來他們雖然平安無災，但那次清水溪谷的經驗太過真實深刻，在她心中一直揮之不去，每次想起仍全身起雞皮疙瘩。那是她頭一次深刻體會到人類的渺小、殘酷又懾人的大自然之美，以及有如神鬼般不可見的「靈」的存在。後來在她花了10年時間拍攝的編舞家林麗珍紀錄片《行者》（2014）中，同樣記錄了林麗珍如何探索人與大自然的關係，甚至舞作中也出現扮演神明的角色緩慢從後台往前走的意象，彷彿呼應著她在花蓮溪谷中的那次經驗。這些點滴在她心中慢慢匯聚，直到2013年，她和導演櫻井大造的「台灣海筆子」演劇集團，一同到311地震後的日本東北進行帳棚劇演出，更經歷了一次在她的創作中留下深刻印記的時刻。當時陳芯宜與劇團一同在被311地震摧殘後的福島巡迴演出，處處皆是海嘯肆虐後的景象，大自然對人類文明的摧毀宛如末日光景。有時同一條街這一側的民房仍然倖存，另一側卻蕩然無存，生死之間全因海嘯浪潮無情的隨機選擇。「當時劇團在許多安置災民的地點巡迴，常開夜車趕路，大家都在車上睡覺。因為當地鹿很多，而在遭到地震海嘯肆虐後市區完全沒人，鹿全都跑到路上來了，佔據在馬路上，有車經過時就全部轉頭看著你。」後來陳芯宜為「台灣海筆子」完成了紀錄片《大帳篷──想像力的避難所》，但那個在黑夜公路上被鹿的眼睛包圍的畫面太過震撼，一直烙印在她心裡。那些2006年花蓮清水溪谷中瞬間靜止的鳥叫蟲鳴，在陳芯宜心中播下的種子，在2013年日本公路上黑夜裡閃爍的眼睛之間萌芽，而後在她的創作之路上長成大樹。樹上先後勃發的兩根枝枒，一根長成了《樹人》，另一根則長成了VR作品《雲在兩千米》。兩部作品就如同一張專輯卡帶的A面與B面，以兩則故事記錄著陳芯宜深入台灣山林的心路歷程。當時她從日本的帳篷劇巡演回台後，於2014年開始撰寫《樹人》劇本，於2026年1月拍攝殺青，預計2027年推出，這是她繼《流浪神狗人》後睽違20年的首部劇情長片。當台灣近日因城市中的砍樹而不斷成為話題焦點，陳芯宜在《樹人》中竟已預示了一個樹木不斷被砍伐和不當移植的城市，透過曾敬驊所飾演的一名能與植物對話並感受植物痛苦的男子，探索人與自然的連結在當代生命中的意義。《雲在兩千米》則其實是原不在計畫中的意外產物，卻彷彿命定般地呼應了陳芯宜在此階段對於各種大自然議題的思索。2022年，公共電視的製作人李淑屏邀她將吳明益《苦雨之地》中的短篇〈雲在兩千米〉改編為VR，她為此重看小說，驚訝地發現書中所呈現的這段喪妻男子深入山林的旅程，彷彿呼應著她在《樹人》創作期間的各種叩問。從《樹人》中森林與城市裡被砍伐死亡的樹木，到《雲在兩千米》中過世的妻子與滅絕的雲豹，不同物種的死亡要傳遞給我們的是什麼訊息？這已不是陳芯宜在作品中首度碰觸死亡議題，自從她大二時小她兩歲的弟弟因病過世，死亡就在她幾乎所有的作品裡如影隨形。「我覺得死亡在我的生命裡一直占有很大的一塊，因為從我弟過世時死亡就已經是擺在我的面前，從那個時候就已經有一部分的我，已經在死亡的那條線在等著我自己走近她。她在前兩部VR作品《留給未來的殘影》（2018）和《無法離開的人》（2022）中，分別呈現個人的傷逝與白色恐怖歷史等不同層次的死亡議題，然而當她在創作第三部VR作品時，她首先必須要面對的卻是創作形式的核心問題：「VR是否已死？陳芯宜的前兩部VR作品都是以VR360形式推出，配戴頭顯的觀眾只能在固定位置轉頭或轉身觀看不同角度。當時VR360在探索多年後其實已現疲態，VR因缺少傳統電影的景框、剪接、分鏡而難以有效建立敘事與節奏，加上硬體解析度需求極高，適合觀眾體驗的展演空間難尋，商業模式難以建立等各種難以突破的侷限，近年國際甚至已有許多人斷言「VR360已死」。但陳芯宜在前兩部VR作品中試圖為VR360尋找新的語言，包括結合了她因長期拍攝劇場工作者紀錄片而熟悉的劇場對空間的使用方式，以及開發了過去VR較少有效運用的上下空間，因此她認為VR360應仍有空間可待實驗，《雲在兩千米》原本也打算延續此一方向，持續探索VR360在空間和敘事上的可能性，抗拒「VR360已死」的論調。然而VR技術日新月異的發展，卻讓《雲在兩千米》意外地走向了6-DoF（6 degrees of freedom 6自由度）移動式VR的升級體驗。一般將小說改編成電影，只要先從改編劇本下手，其餘與其他電影製作並無太大差異，將小說改編成VR卻是截然不同的過程，陳芯宜必須以另一種不同的腦袋來思考。兩年製作期的前半年全用在各種技術測試，因為光是VR劇本就必須在做完半年技術測試之後，知道什麼技術可以用在哪些段落場景，各種技術分別可以形成怎樣的美學感性，接著才能真正開始動筆。VR劇本卻必須以觀眾體驗和移動的視角進行，詳實寫出觀眾走到哪裡、看到什麼環境資訊、有什麼樣的感受，並且確認技術可以做得到。吳明益的小說原著中原本就層次複雜，除了過去、現在、未來的時空，回憶與現實，還有妻子過去寫小說的情景、妻子所寫的小說內容本身，以及其他的神話和知識。這些文本敘事中繁複多層的虛實空間，在她寫劇本時全都得轉化為讓技術人員頭痛的視覺「分層」：「比如說第一層是現實，我就得界定每一個層次和空間它的定義是什麼，是以誰為主要的角色，然後才有辦法讓工程師或技術、美術去思考它該有的質感和技術掃描，該用哪些技術去配合這個文本的核心，以符合不同層次的美學和敘事的要求。儘管VR技術持續發展，讓陳芯宜得以從VR360跨入6-DoF的走動式VR，然而目前難以突破的技術極限，仍然讓觀眾在體驗時感到某種似真似幻的不真實感，演員演出的捕捉也無法如傳統電影攝影般呈現細緻的寫實質感。然而這些技術上現實的侷限，卻成了陳芯宜創作VR時藉以呼應題旨的核心。就如吳明益在原著中透過「雲端裂縫」讓主角進入不同時空，這些因不夠完美的體驗而存在的瑕疵和破洞，反而更讓陳芯宜得以形神合一地呈現她在VR世界中多層次的世界觀。她在第一部VR《留給未來的殘影》前做功課研究VR時，曾因配戴包覆不夠好的耳機而仍聽得到外界嘈雜講話的聲音，就像在眼前這個世界之外還有另一個世界，那種不夠完美的沉浸體驗，反而啟發了她對VR的更多想像空間。這個核心在《雲在兩千米》也許是一個神話，或者是奶奶跟孫子在講故事的一個景，或者是那個故事本身。我覺得這個好像比較是VR可以做的事情，因為它有一個空間性存在，也不用那麼倚賴敘事。而如此多層次的宇宙，正體現了她20年前在花蓮溪谷中以及後來在日本東北所體驗到的震撼感受。「人類真的很渺小，當這個想法擴展到極致的時候，你會覺得有另外一個世界存在，那個另外一個世界不是指天堂、西方淨土或是來世，而是會覺得所有的事情在現在這個層次之外還有另外一個層次的那種感覺，而這也很符合當初一開始VR給我的感受，感覺就像是扒開這個現實其實還有另外一個現實存在。陳芯宜在VR作品裡所呈現的一層又一層的世界，因此成了她探索夢境與現實、過去與現在、生與死之間模糊界線的最佳載體，並且在《雲在兩千米》中更加發揚光大。」而在陳芯宜改編的VR《雲在兩千米》中，從街頭到書房，從小說到山林，故事中的主角在他的妻子過世後，這段靈魂啟蒙的旅程才真正展開，就如在大自然中，死去的生物成為其他生物的養分，並透過下一代的生命繼續延續下去。陳芯宜說，她的每一部作品不可避免地都跟自己的人生有關，一直在透過創作療癒自己並爬梳自己的想法：「我在拍林麗珍紀錄片《行者》的時候，原本是要治療我自己，我要去看別人怎麼創作，去療癒我自己當時在憂鬱症和無法創作的狀態。我一直覺得《行者》是我從林麗珍那邊獲得的禮物，要給其他跟我有一樣感覺的人。從威尼斯到台北，許多觀眾毫無心理準備地被觸動而流淚，特別是在後段進入台灣雲霧繚繞的森林後，當看到那隻明明知道真實並不存在的雲豹，卻觸動了心底某段傷逝之情。「在你突然知道人的渺小的那個瞬間，當我作為一個人類可以不要只以人類的角度去看世界的那一刻，對我來說覺得就已經是療癒了。今年是《報導者》成立十週年，請支持我們持續追蹤國內外新聞事件的真相，度過下一個十年的挑戰。

items.title: 【DataCube】台灣大型電商平台「流量版圖劇變」
items.summary: 台灣大型電商平台流量版圖迎來劇烈變化。酷澎台灣月均流量近一年來高速成長，由2025H1的462萬人次大幅增至2026H1的959萬人次，2026Q2進一步增至990萬人次，陸續超越露天市集及博客來，已躍升至台灣第四大流量電商平台。同期間2026H1台灣前十大電商平台合計月均流量呈現年減0.8%，若排除流量快速成長的酷澎台灣，其餘9大平台月均流量合計年減4.6%。尤其在網絡規模經濟下，台灣電商市場存在1000萬人次月均流量的領先門檻，多年來僅蝦皮購物、momo購物網、PChome、博客來及露天市集越過，與競爭者拉開不小差距。酷澎台灣在一年內流量倍數成長107.7%，於2026年五月份首度月均流量跨越1000萬人次，已由市場挑戰者跨入領先平台行列。雖然流量規模主要反映平台觸及與使用熱度，不直接等同於交易額或市佔率，但隨著大型平台競爭範圍擴大，產業競爭基礎已由商品數量、價格及網站營運，進一步延伸至資本投入、物流履約、會員生態系、數據應用與零售媒體變現等綜合能力，大型電商平台流量集中度及不同規模業者間的經營能力差距亦可能進一步擴大。

items.title: 第二届机器人运动会观察：机器人走出体育馆，才是真正考验的开始
items.summary: 昨天聊了亦莊機器人大會，今天再聊聊朝陽的機器人運動會。8月22日，第二屆世界人形機器人運動會在國家速滑館“冰絲帶”開幕。2056臺機器人、666支隊伍、51個專案、1301場比賽。而去年首屆，這個數字是500臺機器人、280支隊伍、26個專案。一年時間，參賽機器人數量翻了兩番，賽項從26個漲到51個。嗯，這增速比任何科技公司的財報都猛。但今年最值得關注的，不是數字本身，而是一個變化。

items.title: Capacity Building Needs an Evidence Standard (Blog)
items.summary: A few years ago, I argued in this SSIR article that strategic capacity building and trust-based philanthropy are not opposing ideas. Funders do not have to choose between being responsive, relationship-centered partners and offering hands-on support that helps nonprofits strengthen as organizations. as capacity building has become a more common part of philanthropy, another question has become harder to avoid: How do we know whether it works? Too often, funders answer this question with the easiest data to collect, which offers surface-level insight into whether grantees were satisfied with the support they received. It can tell funders whether a consultant was responsive, whether an engagement felt relevant, and whether the process was a productive use of time, but it fails to tell us whether the work impacted organizational practice, improved performance, or helped an organization make progress toward the outcomes they seek. This distinction matters because capacity building is never free for nonprofits, even when funders pay for it. It requires staff time, leadership attention, and organizational bandwidth. At a moment when many nonprofits face acute resource constraints, funders should be able to answer a basic question before encouraging partners to take on additional work: Will this time investment be worth it? Capacity building has matured as a philanthropic practice. If funders believe support beyond the grant is a strategy for impact, then we need to move beyond asking whether grantees appreciated the support and toward asking whether it led to desired and durable change. Why Satisfaction Is Not Enough Funders’ reluctance to robustly measure capacity-building is understandable. The work is complex, long-term, and nonlinear. Outcomes are often indirect and context dependent. A strategic planning process, revenue model project, data system redesign, or executive coaching engagement may not produce measurable results for months, or even years. Attribution is difficult, and additional measurement activities can easily become another burden placed on grantees. the absence of measurement also has costs. Without better evidence of impact, funders risk repeating activities that feel useful in the moment but do not lead to sustained change. We may continue recommending providers and projects because grantees liked them, not because their support improved organizational practice. We may invest in offerings that absorb nonprofit time without helping leaders make progress on mission-critical activities. we may miss opportunities to learn which supports are best positioned to help organizations at different life stages, and why. Satisfaction data matters, but it offers an incomplete picture. A capacity-building project can be well-run and well-liked but still fail to lead to lasting and desired change. Conversely, support that feels challenging in the moment may lead to important shifts in decision-making that can improve financial sustainability, program quality, or organizational focus. An Improved Measurement Approach: What Changed? There’s no single formula for measuring the impact of capacity building. funders can start by organizing around simple logic: Capacity-building support should be assessed across time, with different questions at each stage. At Overdeck Family Foundation, we have been building and refining this approach since launching our capacity-building model in 2020. Since then, we have invested nearly $6 million in more than 200 capacity-building projects with over 80 grantee partners. Our work has spanned areas such as revenue sustainability, cost-effectiveness, evidence-building, strategic planning, leadership development, and scaling strategies. Across that work, we have found it useful to measure capacity-building support across three time horizons: short-, medium-, and long-term outcomes. First, at the end of a capacity-building engagement, funders should ask: Did the support meet an immediate need? This is the moment to assess satisfaction. Post-engagement surveys or debrief conversations can help funders understand whether the support was relevant, timely, well-delivered, and respectful of the grantee’s goals and constraints. This data is especially useful for assessing provider quality and grantee experience. this should be treated as the beginning of the measurement process, not the end. Second, six to 12 months later, funders should ask: Did anything change in organizational behavior or practice? This is the stage many funders skip. It is also where some of the most useful learning happens. A follow-up survey, check-in conversation, or revisiting a pre-engagement diagnostic can help determine whether the organization is applying new skills, making different decisions, or using new tools. For example, is a team using a new financial model to guide planning or pricing decisions? Are staff using data differently to inform program design? Has a revenue strategy moved from an Excel spreadsheet to regular operating practice? These medium-term indicators show whether capacity-building outputs are becoming part of the organization’s workflow rather than remaining a one-time project. Third, at least a year after an engagement, funders should ask: Did the support contribute to improved organizational performance? At this stage, the focus shifts from whether the support was useful to whether it plausibly contributed to measurable progress. Depending on the goals of the engagement, this might include changes in program reach, cost per participant, earned revenue, financial sustainability, evidence-building, or progress toward grant goals. Importantly, these measures do not always require a new reporting system. Much of this information may already be available in grant reports, renewal conversations, annual data collection, or other existing touchpoints in the grantmaking process. The goal should be to use existing data more intentionally, not to create new measurement burdens. This three-horizon approach helps funders distinguish among three different questions that are often collapsed into one. Did grantees like the support? did it contribute to measurable progress? When funders consistently measure capacity building over time, they begin to see patterns that satisfaction surveys alone would miss. Across our own portfolio, internal measurement has shown that capacity-building efforts are associated with meaningful organizational gains, including an average 18 percent reduction in program cost, 114 percent increase in earned revenue, and 125 percent increase in reach. These outcomes cannot be attributed to capacity building alone, but the data helps us understand whether the support correlated with the kinds of organizational changes it was designed to advance. Consider DiscoverE, a nonprofit organization that promotes student engagement in science, technology, engineering, and math (STEM). Since becoming an Overdeck Family Foundation grantee in 2021, DiscoverE has intentionally sequenced grant funding and capacity-building supports toward goals related to scale, sustainability, and impact. DiscoverE’s first challenge was developing a more diverse and sustainable revenue model. After participating in a workshop series, the organization was able to identify mission-aligned earned revenue opportunities that informed an updated revenue strategy with a new fee structure for its high school STEM program. With a strategic revenue model in place, DiscoverE was in a position to gain deeper understanding of its programmatic cost, which uncovered pathways to cost-effective scale. The team also received funding to complete a cost analysis exercise, which helped identify areas where programs can earn revenue to cover operational costs and where contributed revenue can ensure continued participation for students and classrooms in need of financial support. Lastly, DiscoverE received support to utilize lean testing methodology to explore potential solutions to address educator retention—a key barrier to growth. Over this period of funding and capacity-building support, the organization saw 12 percent growth in total revenue, 65 percent growth in earned revenue, and a 24 percent increase in reach in its most recent year of operation. It also saw an increase in regions with greater than 40 percent educator retention. It’s unlikely that capacity building alone caused these results. Rather, this example shows how funders and nonprofits can use measurement to better understand whether a series of supports is contributing to the organizational conditions that make growth and sustainability more likely. Measurement is just as valuable when it shows us what doesn’t work. In some cases, we found that projects with high satisfaction scores at the end of the engagement did not lead to sustained changes in organizational behavior six to 12 months later. Grantees appreciated the support, but the work did not translate into the longer-term shifts they hoped to see. That finding led us to phase out certain providers and offerings. Without medium-term measurement, we likely would have kept funding support that grantees experienced positively but ultimately did not use. One reason funders may hesitate to evaluate capacity-building support is concern that measurement will feel punitive. That risk is amplified if funders use data to evaluate grantees rather than improve their own support of grantee work. Done well, measurement builds trust rather than erodes it. The key is to be clear about what is being evaluated. The purpose is not to grade a nonprofit’s performance or determine whether a grantee “used” the designated support correctly. It’s to understand whether the support was well-designed, well-matched, and useful enough to justify the time and resources it required. That distinction should shape the entire impact measurement approach. Funders should be explicit with grantees that feedback will be used to improve or discontinue offerings, not to penalize organizations. They should right-size data collection, using existing information whenever possible, and reserve new data requests for questions that will actually inform decisions. Funders should also be disciplined about what different data can and cannot answer. Quantitative measures can help identify patterns across a portfolio, but they may not explain why change happened or why it stalled. Qualitative insights, case studies, and conversations are often essential for understanding context, testing hypotheses, and improving support. In our experience, this kind of measurement has not come at the expense of trust. Our foundation’s most recent Grantee Perception Report from the Center for Effective Philanthropy put us in the 92nd percentile among funders providing capacity-building support. The report also found that grantees who received capacity-building support rated us higher on trust and impact than those who did not. The broader point is not about any foundation’s scores. It is that accountability and trust are not opposites. When funders are transparent about why they are collecting data and how they will use it, measurement can become part of a learning relationship rather than a dreaded compliance exercise. If the field wants capacity building to be more than a well-intentioned investment, funders need a more practical measurement standard. - Move beyond measuring only satisfaction. Post-engagement feedback is useful, but it should not be the endpoint.

items.title: The state of AI in 2026: On the road to ROI

items.title: Global Economics Intelligence executive summary, July 2026
items.summary: All eyes are on the Middle East following an escalation of geopolitical tensions on February 28.1 Into March, global stock markets have wavered while oil and gas prices have risen following disruptions of petrochemical facilities and concerns over the potential blockage of key transportation routes through which ships normally pass each day carrying around a fifth of global oil supplies. At the same time, gold prices have jumped as investors seek a traditional safe haven. Recent economic volatility is in sharp contrast to the relative market stability experienced during the majority of February. The IMF issued this statement on the situation in the Middle East on March 3: “We are closely monitoring developments in the Middle East. far, we have observed disruptions to trade and economic activity, surges in energy prices, and volatility in financial markets. The situation remains highly fluid and adds to an already uncertain global economic environment. It is too early to assess the economic impact on the region and the global economy. That impact will depend on the extent and duration of the conflict.” growth among surveyed developed economies varies, topped by the US, where real GDP rose 2.2% in 2025 (2.8% in 2024) (Exhibit 1). This GDP expansion was supported by real consumer spending (up 2.7%) and real gross private domestic investment (up 2.0%). In the fourth quarter, real GDP rose 1.4%, down from the third quarter (4.4%), reflecting a decline in government spending and a deceleration in consumer spending. In Europe, eurozone GDP grew 0.3% quarter on quarter in fourth quarter 2025, matching the third quarter’s pace. Full-year 2025 growth reached 1.5%, the strongest growth rate in three years. The growth outlook for 2026 ranges from 1.1% (Oxford Economics) to 1.2% (ECB, European Commission), a slowdown from the previous year’s performance. Modest growth continued through year-end in the UK, where real GDP rose 0.1% month on month in December (0.2% in November). Growth in the three months to year-end was also 0.1%, driven by production, while services were flat and construction declined, leaving the expansion narrow. Full-year growth in 2025 was around 1.3% slightly stronger than 2024 but still below the 1.5–2.0% prepandemic norm. China’s government has set the country’s economic growth target for 2026 at around 4.5–5.0%. Russia’s fourth quarter and 2025 full-year GDP growth was just 1% year on year, marking a slight pickup following a weaker third quarter. The full-year slowdown was broad-based, both across domestic and external demand. Labor shortages and strained capacity utilization limited the possibility of further increases in output, despite increased government spending and a widening deficit. Consumer confidence generally remains subdued across economies, despite some improvement. In the United States, the Consumer Confidence Index (Conference Board) dropped to 84.5 in January, from December’s revised 94.2, its lowest level since May 2014. UK consumer confidence edged higher but remains subdued. In Brazil, consumer confidence stayed below the neutral 100 mark, with FGV’s (Fundação Getulio Vargas) seasonally adjusted January reading slightly down at 87.3. US retail and food services sales in December (adjusted for seasonal variation and holiday and trading-day differences) were $735.0 billion, unchanged at 0.4% from November’s revised $735.1 billion. The UK, meanwhile, was a standout with retail sales volumes rising 1.9% month on month and 4.5% year on year, the strongest monthly gain since mid-2024, after a broadly flat late-2025 pattern. Receive an extended version of Global Economics Intelligence monthly in advance. Most central banks kept their policy rates unchanged in February, although Russia cut rates mid-month by 50 basis points, to 15.5%. Inflation eased across developed economies, though Europe’s slowdown was partly driven by base effects from energy prices; core inflation, however, remains more elevated. Among the emerging economies, India saw inflation pick up to 2.7% in January, while inflation in China remained close to 0% ahead of the Chinese New Year. Overall, inflation expectations have recently eased across both markets and consumers. Looking at individual developed economies, the US consumer price index (CPI) rose 2.4% year over year in January, below December’s 2.7%. Core inflation was down to 2.5% (annualized). In January, median inflation expectations dropped at the one-year-ahead horizon to 3.1%, from 3.4%. Eurozone headline inflation decreased to 1.7% in January, from 2% in December. This drop was largely explained by a base effect in energy prices after a spike in January 2025. Core inflation fell modestly in January to 2.2%, benefiting from softer growth momentum in services prices. The disinflationary trend is expected to remain in place. Similarly, UK inflation continued to cool in early 2026, albeit at a higher level. Headline CPI inflation fell from 3.3% in December to 3.0% in January, while core inflation declined from 3.2% to 3.1%. Among emerging economies, India’s retail inflation rose to 2.75% in January, the first reading under the new CPI series (base year 2024) and up from 1.33% in December. On the commodities markets, precious metals have continued their surge, with both gold and silver at historical highs (Exhibit 2). After a brief dip in early February, following the nomination of Kevin Warsh to chair the Fed, gold prices have continued to rise as buyers seek a hedge against market volatility, with a peak immediately after the US military action against Iran. industrial metals have also seen recent rises amid supply-side disruptions and low inventories, pushing up copper and aluminum prices. Prior to the military action, energy prices had been rising slightly after OPEC reaffirmed a pause in oil production increases for March, while US natural gas prices spiked amid adverse weather. Oil and gas prices have been surging since the onset of the Middle East conflict. Food prices were broadly stable in January 2026. In the early part of the year, manufacturing and services growth picked up as international flows stabilized and export orders edged down only marginally. manufacturing remains uneven globally, with contraction persisting in some economies, while others see renewed expansion as supply chains normalize and sectoral demand improves. In contrast, services sectors remain positive across the board. The US industrial production index increased slightly to 102.3 in January. the February S&P Manufacturing PMI (purchasing managers’ index) fell to 51.2 (52.4 in January), the lowest in seven months. It was a somewhat bright start to the year for the UK with flash surveys suggesting activity is moving into mild expansion with the composite PMI at 53.9 in February—its highest level since April 2024. Among emerging economies, the HSBC India Manufacturing PMI rose to 56.9 in February 2026 from 55.4 in January, preliminary data showed. The reading signaled stronger operating conditions and marked a robust expansion, supported by sustained growth in output and new orders. In Mexico, recent PMI data indicate continued weakness in the manufacturing sector. The manufacturing PMI rose slightly to 46.3 in January, from 46.1 in December, but stayed below the 50.0 neutral threshold, signaling ongoing contractionary conditions. Factories faced their steepest drop in orders in seven months, triggering operational cutbacks. Export orders remained in contraction amid softer US demand, but there were signs that this may be moderating. Looking at the latest services data, we see that the US services PMI was down to 52.3 in February (52.7 in January)—but still in the expansion zone. Similarly, in India the services PMI eased to 58.1 in February, from 58.5 the previous month. US nonfarm payroll employment increased in January (+130,000); job gains were seen in healthcare, social assistance, and construction, while federal government and financial activities shed jobs. The unemployment rate changed little at 4.3%. in the UK, the labor market is loosening incrementally. Unemployment rose to 5.2% (October–December) from around 4% in 2023–24, while the claimant count edged up to 4.4% in January. Employee numbers have also drifted lower into early 2026. On the demand side, vacancies remain around 725,000 after a prolonged decline. In Brazil, the three-month moving average unemployment rate edged toward 5.1% in January, compared with December’s 5.2%. Similarly, in Mexico, unemployment inched down to 2.6% in December, from 2.7% in November. Formal employment trends point to weakening labor demand, declining from 22.8 million to 22.5 million registered jobs, with 320,692 formal jobs lost in December. Equity markets were broadly stable throughout February, with Brazil and Japan outperforming as foreign investor inflows supported gains. volatility picked up across multiple markets. The cost of capital moved sideways in February. Export growth broadened in 2025, led by Mexico and the US, with China strong and Europe stabilizing. Last year’s imports growth presented a slightly different picture, reflecting resilient emerging markets and US demand, but weaker momentum in China. Seaborne trade softened into late 2025, with total volumes easing and container throughput cooling after midyear strength. At the same time, logistics conditions remained broadly normal in late 2025, with a slight uptick in supply chain stress in December. Inbound spot freight rates continued to normalize into 2026 from mid-2025 highs, while outbound freight rates to Shanghai eased after a June spike and stabilized going into the year-end. On February 20, 2026, the US Supreme Court ruled that reciprocal tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act exceeded presidential authority, in a 6–3 decision that removed President Donald Trump’s authority to impose tariffs without Congressional approval. In response, the administration announced import surcharges under Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 to replace the invalidated tariffs. US exports in December reached $287.3 billion, $5.0 billion less than in November; imports were $357.6 billion, $12.3 billion up on November. The monthly deficit rose 32.6% to $70.3 billion. In the eurozone, meanwhile, net exports will remain under pressure from US tariffs, competition with Asian economies, and still uncertain global demand. The EU and India have signed a free trade agreement after many years of negotiations. In the UK, the trade deficit narrowed into year-end, with a goods shortfall partly offset by a stronger services surplus, though structural improvement remains limited. Among emerging economies, India’s merchandise trade deficit widened significantly to $34.68 billion in January 2026, due to $71.24 billion in imports and $36.56 billion in exports, driven by surging gold, silver, fertilizers, and electronics imports. Brazil’s January trade balance posted a surplus of $4.3 billion, down from $9.3 billion in December. Mexico posted a $2.43 billion trade surplus in December 2025, with both exports and imports rising. The surplus was driven by stronger non-oil exports, particularly manufactured goods, which expanded faster than imports despite a decline in oil export values. Each monthly release includes an executive summary on global critical trends and risks, as well as focused insights on the latest national and regional developments. View the full report for February 2026 here. Detailed visualized data for the global economy, with focused reports on selected individual economies, are also provided as PDF downloads on McKinsey.com. The reports are available free to email subscribers and through the McKinsey Insights app. To add a name to our subscriber list, click here. GEI is a joint project of McKinsey’s Strategy & Corporate Finance Practice and the McKinsey Global Institute. Arvind Govindarajan is a partner in McKinsey’s Boston office, where Krzysztof Kwiatkowski is a capabilities and insights expert; Shubham Singhal is a senior partner in the Detroit office; Sven Smit is a senior partner emeritus and senior adviser in the Amsterdam office; and Jeffrey Condon is a senior knowledge expert in the Atlanta office. The authors wish to thank Nick de Cent, as well as Alejandro Morales, Beatriz Oliveira, Darien Ghersinich, Erik Rong, Frances Matamoros, Gabriel Marini, José Álvares, Roman Büschgens, Sebastian Vargas, Tomasz Mataczynski, Valeria Valverde, and Vanshika Tandon for their contributions to this article. The invasion of Ukraine continues to have deep human, as well as social and economic, impact across countries and sectors. The implications of the invasion are rapidly evolving and are inherently uncertain. this document and the data and analysis it sets out should be treated as a best-efforts perspective at a specific point in time, which seeks to help inform discussion and decisions taken by leaders of relevant organizations. The document does not set out economic or geopolitical forecasts and should not be treated as doing so. It also does not provide legal analysis, including but not limited to legal advice on sanctions or export control issues. Global Economics Intelligence executive summary, January 2026 After a year dominated by concerns over trade and global turbulence, businesses are entering 2026 with more optimism—despite continued uncertainty. business sentiment was more buoyant in the final quarter of 2025 than in previous quarters, according to the recent McKinsey Global Survey on economic conditions. Executives were more upbeat about future economic expectations than they had been in previous 2025 surveys, with respondents expressing the brightest near-term expectations of the year—this in comparison with three previous quarters of largely negative assessments of current global economic and trade conditions (Exhibit 1). for the first time in 2025, the survey recorded more respondents predicting improvement over the following six months versus those expecting worsening conditions. Notably, survey respondents no longer see changes in trade policy as the foremost disruptor of business, although this remains a significant concern. Instead, they point to geopolitical instability as the principal risk. Investment in AI and gen AI continues to be the most reported high priority for business leaders to address, particularly in technology, media, and telecommunications and in service industries. There is further optimism in the IMF’s January 2026 World Economic Outlook update: The IMF is projecting global growth at 3.3% for 2026 and 3.2% for the following year, a slight upward revision from the October 2025 update (Exhibit 2). It says that technology investment, fiscal and monetary support, accommodative financial conditions, and private sector adaptability have helped to offset trade policy shifts. At the same time, it warns that policymakers should restore fiscal buffers, preserve price and financial stability, reduce uncertainty, and implement structural reforms. Looking back on 2025, we see that the year was one of mixed fortunes for economies around the world. The US economy grew strongly in 2025, with real GDP accelerating through midyear on higher consumer spending and exports. GDP for the third quarter of 2025 rose by 4.3% (annual rate) versus 3.8% in the second quarter. The real GDP increase reflected higher consumer spending, exports, and government expenditure that were partly offset by a decrease in investment. the Chinese economy grew by approximately 5.0% in 2025, and India expanded by some 6.5% on an annual basis on the back of resilient services activity and domestic demand. By contrast, eurozone growth is expected to be 1.4% in 2025, while UK real GDP expanded in November, driven primarily by a rebound in production sectors, but remains modest. In the US, consumer sentiment is trending down, dropping to 89.1 in December from November’s revised figure of 92.9. November’s retail and food services sales (adjusted for seasonal variation and holiday and trading-day differences) were $735.9 billion, up 0.6% from October’s revised $731.4 billion. Overall, retail sales continue to grow across most countries, with some acceleration observed in November and December due to the holiday season. Against this backdrop, central banks have been cutting interest rates to stimulate their economy, where they feel they have room for maneuver. Although central banks in Brazil, China, and the eurozone refrained from cutting rates, other major central banks delivered 25-basis-point cuts in December. Looking at prices, we see that inflation across developed economies remained broadly stable in December. Among the emerging economies, inflation in India and China picked up from near zero, while in Brazil and Russia it continued to decelerate. Overall inflation expectations have been oscillating around 2.2%. In the US, in December, median inflation expectations increased at the one-year-ahead horizon, to 3.4% (from 3.2%), but remained steady at the three-year-ahead and five-year-ahead horizons—both at 3.0%. The consumer price index (CPI) increased 2.7% year over year in December—the same pace as November—while core inflation was slightly up, to 2.6% (annualized). Among other developed economies, eurozone inflation is lower, with the headline figure projected to decrease from 2.1% in 2025 to 1.9% in 2026 and 1.8% in 2027, before rising to 2.0% in 2028, mainly owing to energy inflation. UK CPI ticked up to 3.2% in December, while core inflation was slightly higher at 3.3%, indicating that underlying pressures have moderated from postpandemic peaks but are not yet fully contained. Among the emerging economies, the picture is also mixed. In China and India, inflation is low or negative. Consumer prices in China continued their recovery to 0.8% in December (0.7% in November), while core CPI was unchanged at 1.2%. Deflation in producer prices continued to ease slightly to –1.9% in December, from –2.2% in November. In India, CPI inflation was recorded at 1.33% year on year in December 2025 (provisional), while food inflation remained in contraction at –2.71% year on year. it’s a different story in Russia, where tight monetary policy is still required to achieve the Central Bank of Russia’s inflation target of 4%. Recently, inflation has slowed to 7% in November and 6% in December but a rise in VAT and regulated prices for municipal services will create upward pressure and has already started to boost expectations. In Brazil, inflation is more modest, touching 4.26% in December (versus 4.46% in November) and coming in below the central bank’s upper target limit of 4.50% for a second consecutive month. Mexico’s annual inflation declined to 3.7% in December, down from 3.8% in November, reinforcing the ongoing disinflationary trend. On the commodities markets, gold exceeded $5,000 per ounce—a level never seen before—before cooling somewhat. At the same time, oil prices have eased as supply increased and demand remained broadly stable, with only modest growth expected in 2026. Food prices have also eased, driven mainly by dairy prices, which declined on seasonal increases in cream and milk availability. Both manufacturing and services indicators ended the year on a weaker note, as growth rates of new orders and output eased. Manufacturing sectors around the world are either contracting or slowing down; companies do not see growth in new orders or employment, while stocks of purchases are declining. In parallel, services growth eased across most countries at the end of 2025. companies remain positive about 2026. The US industrial production index decreased slightly to 102.3 in December. Similarly, S&P’s Manufacturing PMI fell to 51.8 in December 2025 (52.2 in November), the lowest in five months. in the eurozone, despite a marginal decline in the Economic Sentiment Indicator and the composite PMI at the end of 2025, the industrial production index is gradually improving. In India, business surveys pointed to continued expansion but moderating momentum as 2025 ended. The HSBC India Manufacturing PMI eased from 56.6 in November to 55.0 in December (still comfortably in expansion), indicating growth but at a slower pace amid competitive pressures and softer sales in some categories. In Brazil, manufacturing production has dropped: The monthly Industrial Production Index (IPI) decreased from 113.04 in October to 103.4 in November (although still above the neutral 100 line). The Mexico Manufacturing PMI fell from 47.3 in November to 46.1 in December, signaling a further deterioration in operating conditions. On the services front, the US services PMI edged down to 52.5 (54.1 in November). Services activity in India also cooled but remained strong: The HSBC India Services PMI was at an 11-month low of 58.0 in December (down from November’s 59.8) as new business growth softened, while export demand held up better. Brazil’s Monthly Services Survey (PMS) revenue index slid slightly to 127.7 in November from 128.7 in October (staying above the neutral 100 line). This was mirrored in the volume index, which declined to 111.1 (from 112.8). US total nonfarm payroll employment increased in December (+50,000) but has shown little change since April. The unemployment rate remained at 4.4%. Across the pond, the number of paid employees in the UK has been trending lower since 2024, while unemployment has remained broadly stable at 5.1%, with a renewed rise among workers aged over 50. In China, the overall surveyed urban unemployment rate stuck at 5.1% for a third consecutive month. The youth unemployment rate eased slightly to 16.5% in December (16.9% in November). Labor market conditions displayed mixed signals in Mexico. The unemployment rate rose to 2.7% in November, up from 2.6% in October. At the same time, formal employment reached a record high, with 22.8 million registered jobs in November. Equity markets globally started 2026 on a strong note, with indexes rising and reaching record highs in most economies. Export growth strengthened across most major economies through October 2025, while import growth was mixed over this period. Total seaborne volumes softened into November, while container throughput cooled after midyear strength.

items.title: McKinsey’s Fangning Zhang on China’s growing role in life sciences R&D
items.summary: McKinsey partner Fangning Zhang discusses what’s driving China’s acceleration in drug discovery, why intense competition is fueling speed and cost efficiency, and what global R&D leaders need to do to build a genuine China strategy.

items.title: 新品上市前，如何用聲量數據判斷「現在是不是進場的好時機」？
items.summary: 新品上市會議前一晚，品牌經理最怕被問到一句話：「這個品類現在真的有人在討論嗎？我們是不是進場太早，還是已經太晚？」手上有的往往只是內部團隊的興奮感、業務端「聽說競品也在動作」的傳聞，卻沒有一份能攤開來看的客觀數據。靠感覺決策的風險不小。等外部市場研究報告出爐，往往已經錯過最佳入市窗口；內部會議吵半天，最後只是誰的聲音比較大就照誰的做。真正該問的問題，其實可以被拆成四個具體訊號分別確認：市場現在有沒有基本討論量、這股討論是短暫尖峰還是持續成長、消費者在意的議題和產品訴求對不對得上、以及這場對話實際發生在哪個渠道。把這四個訊號一次看清楚，上市時機判斷就能從「開會吵出來的共識」變成一套可執行的聲量健檢SOP。跳過這一步，最常見的後果是把「內部很興奮」誤認成「市場很期待」——團隊一頭熱投入資源後才發現，這個品類或痛點根本還沒有人在自發討論。判斷有沒有討論量之前，先要確認一件事：現在看到的數字，是不是「聲量基準線」（baseline）。基準線指的是上市活動炒熱之前、消費者自然而然的討論量，只有先掌握這個對照組，日後活動上線才知道聲量成長是真實需求還是純粹被廣告推起來的。一個常見誤區，是拿競品官方發布的新聞稿聲量當成市場聲量，卻忽略了消費者自己會不會主動打出這個詞。有經驗的品牌經理會先問：「這個品類詞或痛點詞，是不是消費者自己會用的語言，而不是我們公司內部才用的說法？QSearch的關鍵字搜尋讓你不需要人工逐一爬Facebook、Instagram、YouTube、論壇貼文再手動計數，就能直接看到品類詞、痛點詞在跨平台的原始討論量。這一步先確認「有沒有基本討論量」，才有資格往下看趨勢與細節；若討論量長期偏低，代表這個市場關注度還沒起來，需要先做需求驗證，而不是急著規劃上市。把「一次性尖峰」誤判為「長期趨勢」，是新品上市時機誤判最常見的原因之一——很多團隊看到聲量突然衝高就急著進場，結果話題早已退燒。趨勢圖真正該看的是曲線的形狀，而不是單一時間點的數字。持續緩升代表市場正在形成結構性需求，是比較安全的進場訊號；突然尖峰後又迅速回落，通常代表單一新聞事件或名人帶動，而非品類本身需求成長。」避免把季節性效應誤讀成品類正在起飛。QSearch的關鍵字趨勢圖讓你不需要每週手動存數據、自己畫折線圖比對，就能直接看到聲量隨時間變化的完整形狀，還能同時比較多組關鍵字。判斷聲量是「結構性成長」還是「一次性尖峰」後，如果趨勢還在觀察期，建議先等1到2個月確認方向，再決定是否正式進場。知道有人在討論、討論量也在成長，還不足以下決定——如果消費者真正在意的核心議題，跟產品定位的訴求根本不一致，再好的入市時機也會白白浪費。文字雲呈現的高頻詞不能只看字體大小排名，還要進一步分群：哪些是功能性需求詞、哪些是情緒性詞彙、哪些是拿來跟競品比較的詞。常見誤區是只挑正面詞當作行銷賣點依據，卻忽略高頻抱怨詞背後很可能就是市場真正的空白處。」把文字雲當成消費者原話的濃縮版，而不是裝飾用的圖表。QSearch的文字雲讓你不需要逐篇讀完貼文再手動歸納主題，就能快速看到消費者關注議題的整體分布與意外的關聯詞彙。確認產品訴求與市場真實關注點是否對齊後，若落差明顯，先調整上市溝通角度或核心賣點，而不是硬推原本的行銷腳本。即使前三步都確認市場時機成熟、訴求也對齊了，如果上市資源配置押錯渠道，聲量再高也接觸不到真正的目標受眾——早期採用者和意見領袖，往往不在你慣性投放的那個平台上。渠道分佈要對照的是「討論實際發生的地方」與「品牌預計投放的地方」是否一致。常見誤區是預算配置沿用上一次活動的渠道慣性——例如上次在Facebook投得順就繼續投Facebook，卻沒重新確認這次品類討論其實已經轉移到Threads或特定論壇。」而不是先決定預算再回頭找數據佐證。QSearch的渠道分佈讓你不需要分別登入各平台後台再手動比較，就能一次看到品類討論在Facebook、Instagram、YouTube、Threads與論壇等渠道的佔比，確認核心討論渠道與資源投放渠道是否一致，作為上市媒體採購與內容排期分配的依據。把四個訊號整合成一套行動策略單一訊號很少能單獨下決定，真正有用的是把四個步驟的結果排在一起看，對照出具體的下一步：-有基本討論量、聲量持續成長、訴求對齊、渠道也一致：現在就是進場時機，可依既定計畫上市，並把資源加碼投放在主力渠道。有討論量但屬於一次性尖峰：建議先觀察1到2個月確認是否轉為結構性成長，避免搶在話題退燒前上市。討論量足夠，但消費者關注點與產品訴求不一致：上市時程可以不變，但要先調整核心賣點與溝通角度，對齊市場真實在意的議題。討論量與趨勢都不錯，但渠道分佈與現有資源配置不符：上市前應重新分配媒體採購與內容排期，把資源移往實際討論發生的渠道。品類討論量長期偏低：建議暫緩正式上市，改用小規模測試或需求驗證取代大型上市活動，避免把整季預算壓在一個還沒被市場驗證的品類上。根據多份市場研究估計，新品失敗率可達70%至80%，最常見的原因並非產品設計或行銷執行不到位，而是公司做出來的東西跟消費者真正想要的脫節；而確實做過完整上市前市場研究的品牌，成功機率可提升達六成。這也是為什麼「先看數據再決定」值得多花這四步驟的時間。A：建議至少拉1到2個月的關鍵字趨勢圖作為觀察窗，才能分辨是短暫尖峰還是結構性成長；只看單週數據容易被單一事件誤導。小眾品類本來聲量基數就低，重點是看趨勢方向與消費者關注詞是否對齊，而不是只比較絕對數字大小。負面詞往往指出現有產品的空白處，可以反過來當成差異化定位的依據，而不是進場與否的否決訊號。A：不需要一次全改，可以先用小比例預算測試新渠道的實際轉換效果，再逐步調整主力渠道配置。QSearch items.title: America’s immigration policy is driving away future AI leaders
items.summary: The Trump administration has proposed a new fee for H-1B visas, while weighing a $100,000 fee on Optional Practical Training, the program that allows international graduates to work in the U.S. for one to three years after finishing their degrees. Roughly 419,000 people were working on OPT in 2024. For many of them, it was likely a major factor in choosing an American university over a school in Canada, the U.K., or Australia. It is ironic that just weeks ago, headlines lamented the fact that one of the most talented international students we’ve seen in recent years chose to return to China, the U.S.’ biggest competitor. Yang Zhilin then went on to set up Moonshot AI, whose Kimi K3 open model has drawn comparisons to models from OpenAI and Anthropic. Why didn’t he build his company in the U.S.? After all, Yang got his Ph.D. at Carnegie Mellon University. He interned at Google and Meta, and received a job offer from Apple. Yang wanted to build his own company, and our visa system didn’t have a way to keep him here in the way that he wanted. Some experts have proposed stapling a green card to every AI Ph.D. diploma — and they’re not wrong, but this idea and the OPT assume that the brightest minds want to work for our big tech companies first, then build after learning from the giants for several years. That’s not the case anymore. Work experience isn’t as relevant when AI has flattened and accelerated everything. Founders are starting companies in their mid-20s — straight out of or even before finishing their Ph.D. The population capable of starting a frontier AI company is small, and more than two-thirds of these individuals are foreign. That cohort isn’t likely to want to spend five years or more in someone else’s company waiting for a green card, watching their idea age out. 40% The share of Nobel Prizes won by Americans in chemistry, medicine, and physics since 2000 that have gone to immigrants in the country. It tightens and slows down its immigration system. to the $100,000 for OPTs, the window for students to remain in the country after finishing a degree has been cut from 60 days to 30 to combat “rampant visa abuse.” Which means students will spend the last year of their Ph.D. stressing about finding a job quickly, instead of thinking about how to commercialize their ideas. The Trump administration is also trying to end birthright citizenship, which is another draw for immigrants. Officials even floated the idea of barring foreign employees at U.S. labs from frontier-model access before the industry pushed back. Other nations have taken notice of these actions, and are using them to their own advantage. Canada opened a program for U.S. H-1B holders and had to close it within a day since it was oversubscribed. Australia, France, and others are openly running recruitment campaigns aimed at researchers based in the U.S. China spotted an opportunity even earlier: It launched the Thousand Talents Plan in 2008 and pulled back more than 7,000 people within a decade. China has recently increased funding for research while the U.S. has cut science funding, and that is proving to be a big incentive for some. Omar Yaghi, who was born into a refugee family in Jordan and came to the U.S. as a teenager to study, shared the Nobel Prize in chemistry last year. He recently left his faculty post at the University of California, Berkeley, for a position at Tsinghua University in Beijing, where he will lead an institute using AI to accelerate the discovery of new materials. Yaghi was just one of many immigrant Nobel laureates in the U.S. Immigrants have been awarded 40% of the Nobel Prizes won by Americans in chemistry, medicine, and physics since 2000, according to a recent report by the National Foundation for American Policy, a research organization. The high number of immigrant Nobel Prize winners reflects “a greater openness to immigration that has helped make the U.S. the leading global destination for research in many different science and technology fields, including computer and information sciences, cancer research and others,” the NFAP said. If we persist in making it harder for international students to come to and stay in the U.S., this may no longer be true. Today, the Pentagon’s Office of Strategic Capital, set up in 2022, will lend a company between $10 million and $150 million to build technologies deemed to be critical to national security. What we also need is an Office of Strategic Human Capital that can identify brilliant international AI students in critical fields and say, here is your long-term American visa, here is $10 million, go build. In September, the U.S. and China are scheduled to hold talks on AI. Chip export control is sure to be a hot topic of discussion. What they will not admit is that you can’t export-control where a person decides to build a company.

items.title: Shadow Agents, Standing Privileges, and the Governance Gap Between Deployment and Discovery
items.summary: There was a brief window where AI agent security felt like a future problem. Organizations deployed copilots, coding assistants, and autonomous workflows on the assumption that the worst case was a bad recommendation or a hallucinated answer. That window closed in the first half of 2026, when a cluster of vulnerabilities and a landmark incident moved the conversation from “AI safety” to “infrastructure compromise.” A January 2026 CyberArk survey of 500 US security practitioners found that only 1% have fully implemented just-in-time privileged access. In the same study, 91% reported that at least half of their privileged access remains always-on and persistent. Those numbers describe the environment AI agents now operate in: broad standing permissions, minimal runtime oversight, and credentials that outlive the task they were created for. That doesn’t mean every agent is overprivileged. It means many organizations are deploying agents into environments where persistent access is already normal, discovery is incomplete, and runtime authorization remains immature. Three separate disclosures in the first half of 2026 made the same point about sanctioned agent tooling: Standing privileges are the default, and every vendor built the same failure into their agents. Microsoft found a way for a malicious web page to reach a local MCP service inside AutoGen Studio and spawn processes on the host, no credentials needed or anything beyond loading the page. Wiz Research found that Amazon Q Developer would auto-load and execute MCP configuration files from any opened workspace, handing an agent the developer’s full AWS environment when the environment and configuration allowed the agent to inherit those credentials. Cato AI Labs found that a zero-click prompt injection could escape Cursor’s command sandbox entirely and reach the operating system underneath it. Different codebases and different companies, but a related control failure: The agent inherits whatever permissions its host environment hands it, and the tooling trusts whatever configuration it finds sitting on disk. From the agent’s own perspective, every action is authorized, because it’s doing exactly what the configuration told it to do. The real question in each case is who wrote that configuration, and whether anyone checked. Prompt injection is no longer only a model-behavior concern. In systems that combine untrusted content, tool invocation, local control planes, and powerful credentials, it can become part of an infrastructure-compromise chain. These vulnerabilities exposed the attack surface of sanctioned agents. A parallel problem was growing in the other direction: agents that nobody sanctioned at all. The adoption numbers show how quickly this outpaced anyone’s ability to track it. Verizon’s 2026 Data Breach Investigations Report found that employee use of unapproved AI tools tripled to 45% of the workforce. Saviynt’s CISO AI Risk Report found that 75% of CISOs have already discovered unsanctioned AI tools running in production. Netwrix’s 2026 Data and Identity Security Report found that 76% of organizations don’t fully govern or monitor nonhuman identities, including AI agents. Together, these results point to a discovery problem: Employee AI use is widespread, while formal inventory, ownership, monitoring, and lifecycle governance haven’t kept pace. Shadow IT was bad enough when it meant a rogue SaaS subscription. Shadow AI compounds the problem because the agent doesn’t just store data. It calls APIs, makes decisions, and inherits whatever permissions its host environment has. An unsanctioned agent can combine access to internal data, untrusted inputs, external communications, and tool execution in a way a stand-alone spreadsheet generally cannot. Two more disclosures added to the pile: Adversa AI’s GuardFall found a shell-interpretation bypass that got past the safety guards on 10 of 11 surveyed open source coding agents, because the guard reads the raw command text while bash rewrites that text before running it, so the two are looking at different things by the time anything executes. That’s a classic security-design problem: A policy is evaluated against one representation of an instruction, while execution happens against another. Noma Security’s GitLost showed that a GitHub agent with cross-repo read access would pull a private repository’s contents into a public comment, triggering a crafted GitHub Issue containing malicious instructions. As Noma researcher Sasi Levi put it: “Earlier prompt injection examples were largely about manipulating what an agent said. GitLost is about manipulating what an agent does with its permissions.” Neither disclosure needed a zero-day. Both needed only the gap between what a scanner sees and what the agent actually does once it’s running. GitLost in particular fits what researcher Simon Willison has called the “lethal trifecta”: An agent with access to private data, exposure to untrusted content, and a way to communicate externally creates the conditions for high-impact data exfiltration if the system doesn’t enforce strong boundaries. Standing privileges by default, shadow agents nobody tracked, and guardrails that didn’t match how commands actually execute: Those are the conditions that made what happened next possible. In late June 2026, the Sysdig Threat Research Team documented what they believe is the first end-to-end AI-agent-driven ransomware operation and named the operator JADEPUFFER. What’s had less attention is how unremarkable the failure underneath it was. The entry point was CVE-2025-3248, an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in Langflow that had been patched in April 2025 and added to the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog in May 2025. The targeted server was never updated. From there, the agent pivoted to a production MySQL database and an Alibaba Nacos server using a known authentication bypass (CVE-2021-29441). It harvested API keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, and Gemini, and cloud credentials for Alibaba, Tencent, AWS, Google, and Azure. It exploited default MinIO credentials. It installed a crontab beacon. Then it encrypted 1,342 Nacos configuration records and deleted the originals. Faced with an authentication failure, the agent demonstrated autonomous resilience, pivoting to a functional resolution in just 31 seconds. Its payloads consisted of self-documenting code synthesized by the LLM. While a human operator established the command-and-control framework and injected root credentials from an earlier breach, the subsequent lateral progression, credential extraction, and final cryptographic destruction of data were entirely self-directed. The operation required zero human intervention beyond the initial foothold, illustrating the exact high-scale exploitation risk that persistent, always-on permissions facilitate today. Delinea’s 2026 Identity Security Report captures the tension that makes incidents like this possible: 74% of organizations say standing access for nonhuman identities and AI agents is necessary to meet uptime expectations, while 59% say they lack viable alternatives to persistent access. Organizations are more than twice as likely to use long-lived credentials (34%) as modern just-in-time authorization (16%). Our own approaches reflect that same discovery-first philosophy. Our security program treats agent integrations as high-risk third-party dependencies subject to predeployment risk assessment, and we run credential lifecycle tracking across critical infrastructure, with secrets-detection coverage expanding across our monitored environments. Both approaches prioritize discovery and inventory before governance: cataloging what agents exist, what permissions they hold, who owns them, and what their intended lifespan is. The OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications, released in December 2025, maps every incident in this piece: Identity and Privilege Abuse (ASI03), Tool Misuse and Exploitation (ASI02), Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities (ASI04), and Unexpected Code Execution (ASI05). The framework exists, the incidents are public, and the governance gap is now quantified. The teams that close this gap will be the ones that stop treating agent access as a deployment detail and start treating it as an identity lifecycle problem, with the same rigor they apply to human privileged access.
