items.title: 读书笔记2693：山外山 (评论: 山外山)
items.summary: 讀書筆記2693：山外山讀書筆記2693：山外山上一次讀外國人寫中國專題的書如此舒心的還是史先生寫的前朝夢憶，他們一致的地方是把人物和時代微縮在了一個盆栽之中，高屋建瓴，細節處又栩栩如生，讀這樣的書就是最好的享受，翻譯也是功不可沒。中國的任何玩意都是有圈子的，鄙視鏈始終存在，文無第一武無第二，最簡單的自然就是看價格，以前書畫行情好，齊白石價格高，徒子徒孫也佔便宜，現在藝術品溢價散去，好多人的價格就跳水了，陳先生在道教學裡就說過，他們這行當，兩類作者各有利弊，道門中人熟悉內部暗語，但存在門第之見，學者寫書容易站在門檻外，始終是門外漢。書法圈就是如此，我們讀鍾繇（yao）他們一定要讀鍾由，你發音，你就暴露了不是門內人，就受鄙視了。明代承接的是南宋院體和浙派，隨著蘇州成為當時文化中心，吳門崛起，掌握了話語權，同古琴一樣，浙派在那個時候都沒落了，現在的所謂浙派古琴同宋毫無關係。到明晚期董其昌成為了領軍人物，他就說蘇州這邊大家都搞商業繪畫，偽作贗品橫行，對畫家的提升形象很大。經常去蘇州出差，去年江老爺子也過世了，見證了蘇州古舊書的興衰，哪怕在上海崛起之後，蘇州也一直是古琴，古舊書，書法繪畫的中心，人才輩出。很多年前路過深圳大芬村，歎為觀止，商業油畫全球大部分都是這裡出品的，很多技工水平很高，要是臨摹梵高的畫作，專業畫家也搞不過他們。曾經畫派的紛爭已經過去了，孰強孰弱自有徒子徒孫爭辯，再不濟也可以按照市場價格定屬性，芸芸眾生的我們讀讀高先生的故事，看看插圖和窗外的風景就夠了。

items.title: Architectural Guardrails for AI-Generated Code
items.summary: Consider a composite of a failure pattern that’s becoming increasingly common on teams that have scaled AI-assisted development past a handful of enthusiasts. A staff engineer named Priya opens a pull request. The PR is 340 lines and adds an endpoint that writes to the customer table directly, bypassing the internal customer service API. The AI coding agent that wrote it has been the team’s most productive contributor for six months. The reviewer, three months into the team, approves. The PR ships that afternoon. Two weeks later, during an integration debug, someone notices that customer records written by that endpoint are missing audit-log entries. The audit hooks live in the customer service API. The team banned direct database access two years ago for exactly this reason and wrote an architectural decision record (a versioned markdown document, one of dozens the team has accumulated, that captured what was decided, why, and what was superseded) to memorialize the rule. The engineer who wrote the ADR has since left. Nobody on the current team remembered the decision. The document was sitting in a directory the current workflow never touches. The team spends most of a sprint on cleanup. Nobody calls this a failure of AI-assisted development. The AI wrote functional code. It just wrote code that violated a decision the team had already made, in a document the AI had no view into. This is a specific failure mode. It is not a hallucination since the output was grounded, syntactically valid, and idiomatic. It’s not a model-quality problem since a better model on that same prompt wouldn’t necessarily help if the decision remained absent from its context. Not the model-internal sense of context window, but the organizational sense. The ADR was available in the repository. It was never surfaced to the agent, and the reviewer had not read it. This piece is about naming what would need to exist for that PR to have been caught, or better, never written in the first place. Priya’s PR illustrates one source of a broader rework problem. Faros AI, an engineering analytics platform, published a report in 2026 based on telemetry from more than 22,000 developers across 4,000+ teams. AI-code acceptance rates had risen from 20% to 60% between periods of low and high AI adoption, while code churn (i.e., lines deleted within days of being added) had increased 861% over the same interval. Faros is careful in how it frames the churn number. The increase may include not only rework but productive refactoring, previously unaffordable cleanup, or faster iterative improvement. the number still exposes a gap between code entering the repository and code that survives there. A gap that has widened, at scale, alongside AI adoption. Anecdotally, engineers at teams running these tools describe returning to code they had already approved to fix issues that were not obvious at review time. Architectural drift, i.e., code that individually looks fine but collectively pulls the codebase away from where the team agreed it should go, is one plausible contributor. The pattern-matching explanation for that gap has been that the AI isn’t good enough at writing code yet, and a better model will close it. Watch enough review cycles at a team running AI-assisted development for a year, though, and a different pattern emerges. The generated code isn’t obviously bad. What it doesn’t do is respect decisions the team has recorded but the AI has never seen. Why current tools sit at the wrong layer Teams commonly reach for several existing mechanisms to close this gap. Most of them are the wrong shape for the problem. The closest attempts are files like Cursor Rules and CLAUDE.md, i.e., free-text markdown documents dropped into the project root so agents read them as standing instructions. These are the right instinct at the wrong resolution. Free text has no precedence rules, no versioning, no lifecycle. When one rule contradicts another, nothing arbitrates. When a rule is violated, nothing catches it. These are documents in the shape of configuration. Linters and code formatters operate a layer below. They enforce that a function has a return type annotation or that a variable name follows a convention. They can’t enforce that customer-data writes must go through the customer service API, because that’s not a syntactic property. It’s a semantic decision recorded in a document the linter has no reason to read. Dependency scanners, SCA tools, and lockfile audits close a related gap; they catch known vulnerable libraries, license violations, and outdated versions. They would’ve flagged nothing about Priya’s PR. Every dependency in it was current, invulnerable, and blessed. The violation was a routing choice inside the team’s own architecture, not a library problem. LLM-assisted code review is the fashionable answer. A second AI reads the pull request and comments on it. This catches surface issues like a swallowed exception, an off-by-one bug. It doesn’t catch drift, however, because the second AI has the same problem as the first: no durable access to the team’s recorded decisions. Two probabilistic passes over the same blind spot are not one deterministic pass with sight. Human review is the last line, and it works when the reviewer knows the history and has enough time to inspect the change. Agentic development changes both conditions. Agents can produce multiple implementations, pull requests, and revisions in the time it takes a human reviewer to assess one. Code output scales; review attention does not. Asking humans to compensate by reviewing more and harder simply moves the constraint downstream. None of these tools are bad. They’re just the wrong layer for the drift problem. What the missing layer would need to do The missing layer connects recorded engineering decisions to the tools that generate, review, and merge code. Its job is to make the team’s accumulated architectural decisions machine-readable, -injectable, and -enforceable. I’ll call this layer engineering governance, borrowing the term from adjacent categories like data governance and security governance, where it means the same thing: A structured way for an organization to make explicit and enforceable the rules it already implicitly follows. At the shape level, the layer needs to do four things. - It needs to hold decisions in a structured corpus with precedence and lifecycle metadata so that a tool knows which ADR wins when two conflict, and which decisions are still active. - It needs to retrieve from that corpus reliably, so the same code produces the same set of relevant decisions each time. - It needs to inject those decisions into the AI’s context before the agent writes code, so the output accounts for them rather than needing to be caught afterwards. - It needs to enforce them in continuous integration, blocking or flagging code that violates them, with the verdict traceable to a specific ADR, a specific term that matched, a specific rule. The critical property that ties those four together is a discipline about where probabilistic reasoning is allowed. Probabilistic systems may retrieve or recommend. They shouldn’t independently determine an enforcement verdict. Every block or warning has to reconstruct from artifacts on disk. That’s the code, the ADR, the retrieval log, the rule text. Doing so when a developer then asks “why did this fail?” or an auditor asks “on what basis?” results in the answer not being “the AI said so.” That’s what makes the layer defensible in the situations where defensibility matters: regulated environments, compliance review, incident retrospectives, and the everyday conversation where an engineer has to justify a blocked merge to the person whose code was blocked. AI may help surface relevant decisions, but it shouldn’t be the final authority. The enforcement path must remain deterministic: every verdict should resolve to explicit rules, observable evidence in the code, and a result that another person can reproduce. Naming a category clearly requires naming what falls outside it. The engineering governance layer, done right, is not any of the following: Nothing iteratively deciding what to do next. The layer runs when called, produces a verdict, and stops. - Memory in the retrieval-augmented-generation sense. Retrieval methods can vary and may be probabilistic; the enforcement verdict cannot. The corpus of decisions is the source of truth. - Code reviewed by AI. Reviewing generated code with a second model doesn’t address the underlying problem, which is that the first model had no access to the team’s decisions. Production teams increasingly run Cursor, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, and Codex in parallel, sometimes on the same repository. They may also use open-weight or self-hosted models for sensitive codebases and internal workflows. Engineering governance must remain independent of both the coding tool and the underlying model, so the same architectural decisions and deterministic enforcement apply across them all. The AI coding stack is assembling itself in the open, without anyone architecting it. Each of the major coding assistants is specializing on a different piece of the loop; editing, autonomous execution, review, planning. The layer this stack doesn’t yet have is engineering governance, and until it does, three consequences follow. The need isn’t limited to regulated industries. Any team that values reliable engineering, long-term product quality, and the trust of its customers needs to know that generated code respects the decisions the system depends on. In higher-risk environments, that requirement becomes formal and auditable. Elsewhere, it’s simply part of building software responsibly. In both cases, the enforcement path should be deterministic and traceable, with the rules, evidence, and verdict open to inspection rather than hidden inside another model or a proprietary black box. For engineering leaders reading this today Priya’s PR is a pattern, not an incident. Three things worth doing this quarter, regardless of tooling choices. - Audit your architectural decision records. Do they explicitly name the decisions they replace? If your team doesn’t write ADRs, this is the moment to start.

items.title: “I just chose words carefully”
items.summary: “I just chose words carefully.” I don’t think anyone particularly enjoys typesetting in monospace. Regular text is okay – at least as okay as it can be: Right aligning is also fine, as long as you don’t mind counting spaces, but centering already gets tricky, as you don’t have a half space to make things truly even: full justification is where things get particularly weird. The spaces are just too large, and cannot be distributed evenly, creating a really unpleasant feeling: The solution used in typesetting elsewhere is hyphenation, but in monospace hyphenation also feels unpleasant, with the hyphens drawing too much attention to themselves (and subsequently messing up copy and paste): This is why you don’t see full justification in text files very often. there is one more option. You can rewrite the text to choose only words that precisely add up to the line length to avoid any double spaces. This is exactly what rs1n did in the late 1990s for his guide to Super Metroid: It’s astonishing, as it goes like this on for 17,000 more words, each right margin perfectly ending on a letter, no twin spaces in sight. The author lightly covers in the FAQ at the bottom: What program did you use to justify the text? I just chose words carefully so that everything lined up on the right hand side. Everything was done with an ASCII editor. I’m sharing this mostly as a curiosity; some rewrites for physical books are par the course to avoid widows and orphans, but you don’t see them as much in onscreen writing.

items.title: 正崴切割森崴能源，每股 0.05 元出售持股、9 月完成交割
items.summary: 正崴與旗下永崴投控決定出售森崴能源持股，擬以每股0.05元參與公開收購案，預計9月14日完成交割。受到台電離岸風電二期工程鉅額虧損影響，正崴表示，考量後續風險仍可能持續擴大，因此決定處分森崴持股，交易完成後將喪失對森崴能源的控制力。正崴集團合計持有森崴能源約1.43億股，其中永崴投控持有約1.21億股。森崴能源自2025年第二季以來，受到旗下富崴能源承接台電離岸風電二期工程成本大幅追加影響，出現鉅額虧損，截至今年6月30日，每股淨值已降至森崴海外子公司新加坡寶崴進入清算程序，森崴也因此認列相關清算損失，部分銀行並要求提前還款。由於台電離岸風電二期工程後續仍存在工程款、追加款等協商事項，正崴認為未來風險仍難以控制，因此正崴與永崴投控決定透過參與公開收購、應賣持股的方式，降低後續持續認列虧損、影響股東權益的風險。依公開收購時程，本次應賣截止日為9月7日，預計9月14日完成交割。若最終應賣股數超過預定收購數量，公開收購人將依相同比例向所有應賣人收購，因此正崴與永崴投控最終實際成交股數及交易金額，仍須待公開收購完成後才能確定。至於森崴能源目前面臨的債務問題，正崴協理羅奇瑋表示，目前相關借款規模估計約169億元，森崴先前已向銀行聯貸委員會申請債務協商並獲通過，後續仍將持續與銀行進行協商。羅奇瑋也說明，正崴與永崴投控處分森崴能源持股，並不代表森崴既有債務隨股權交易移轉給公開收購人。 請參閱所附表格 ↛

items.title: 毫米波模組通吃國防、衛星大單！稜研科技 9 月登創新板掛牌上市
items.summary: 稜研科技明日將舉辦創新板上市前業績發表會，預計９月掛牌交易，董事長張書維表示，稜研目前技術已獲多家Tier-1客戶認證，目前已正式進入產品導入與放量期，隨著寬頻通訊、國防與多軌衛星三大應用陸續推進，毫米波相控陣列天線模組業務正由研發驗證全面走向商用交付。張書維表示，稜研科技成立自2014年，自2018年起確立以5G與衛星通訊為核心發展方向，產品涵蓋天線模組、測試設備及系統解決方案，串接晶片、射頻前端與終端應用，並以「儀器設備」及「天線模組」兩大主軸，建立涵蓋研發驗證、產品開發到系統整合的完整解決方案。張書維指出，國際電信聯盟（ITU）2026年確立6G技術性能指標，涵蓋AI、沉浸式通訊與整合感知等六大場景，而具備高頻、大頻寬與精準波束控制特性的「毫米波」與「相控陣列技術」，已成為5G/6G、衛星通訊及國防雷達不可或缺的關鍵基礎技術。張書維分享，隨著國防、多軌衛星與行動通訊市場陸續推進，稜研毫米波天線模組邁入商用量產與實際交付階段，而在5G/6G通訊固定無線接入（FWA）領域，稜研以相控陣列天線模組供應商角色，參與新興市場電信商的大型毫米波專案，更已成為少數合格供應商之一。多軌衛星領域方面，張書維指出，，稜研與美商Comtech合作開發「One Modem, One Antenna」多軌道使用者終端，以單一天線與數據機架構支援不同軌道衛星系統間的切換，目前已完成多顆在軌衛星的端對端連線測試，並進一步洽談在地組裝代工，朝商用出貨邁進。從營收結構來看，張書維指出，天線模組已成為稜研重要的成長動能，從2024年占營收比重約5.62%，提升至2025年的30.30%，目標2027年突破50%，並隨著國防專案陸續由驗證階段邁入交付與量產，可望帶動天線模組營收持續攀升，預期2027年整體營收可望維持高雙位數成長。 請參閱所附表格 ↛

items.title: 光進銅退趨勢加速，崇越攜手日本 SCIVAX 布局 CPO 光學元件量產
items.summary: 隨著生成式AI與全球高速運算基礎設施的蓬勃發展，資料中心對能量效率與頻寬密度的要求大幅攀升，傳輸能耗劇增已成為高速晶片發展面臨的巨大瓶頸。半導體及光電關鍵材料整合服務廠商崇越科技精準掌握「光進銅退」的產業趨勢，攜手日本奈米壓印技術（Nanoimprint Lithography, NIL）領航者SCIVAX，全力搶攻高頻寬、低能耗的「共封裝光學技術」（Co-Packaged Optics, CPO）關鍵商機。相較於傳統的可插拔式光學模組，CPO架構因具備更短的電性傳輸路徑、更低的功耗、更高的頻寬密度以及更佳的散熱效率，被視為克服傳輸能耗瓶頸的典範轉移技術。9月4日上午11點，崇越科技在SEMICON Taiwan的TechXPOT舞台進行「迎接光進銅退時代：奈米壓印在光通訊和CPO的關鍵應用」技術發表，向全球客戶展示從光學模擬設計到高精度晶圓級壓印量產的一站式解決方案。迎戰AI與高算力需求「光進銅退」推動CPO架構變革崇越科技首席執行長陳德懿表示，隨著人工智慧與高效能運算（HPC）數據量爆發性成長，傳統銅導線傳輸面臨頻寬限制與高耗能挑戰，CPO將光學引擎與邏輯晶片共同封裝於同一基板上，能顯著縮短電路傳輸距離、降低功耗，並大幅提升頻寬密度與能源效率。在此關鍵架構轉折點上，高精度且具備量產優勢的光學元件製造技術成為CPO普及的核心。透過搭配日本信越化學（Shin-Etsu Chemical）的高可靠度光學材料，所製成的微透鏡陣列（Microlens Array）具備極佳的耐熱性與高光訊號耦合效率，確保在高密度封裝與高熱運作環境下，仍能保持極佳的光傳輸品質，展現光學元件微型化與高效能製造的堅強實力。經嚴格測試證實，在極端溫差循環與熱應力下，該光學透鏡不產生任何剝離或龜裂，完美確保了在高熱環境下的傳輸穩定性與長期信賴性。現場也將同步展出厚度小於60微米（μm）、不需玻璃基板的自支撐型微透鏡陣列，能在極度微型化的受限空間中，提供極佳的光學耦合傳輸效能。為滿足快速變化的光通訊與AI晶片市場需求，SCIVAX具備專利壓印技術，能大幅縮短光學元件「從設計到製造」的開發週期。在產能佈局方面，SCIVAX於富山市擁有兩座晶圓代工基地，8吋晶圓月產能可達8,000片。 請參閱所附表格 ↛

items.title: 傳軟銀子公司祭 55 億美元權證，爭取 OpenAI 資料中心合約
items.summary: 華爾街日報披露，日本軟銀集團（SoftBank）旗下子公司SB Energy籌備首次公開募股（IPO）之際，已向OpenAI提供價值約55億美元認股權證，盼爭取這位資料中心客戶。華爾街日報（The Wall Street Journal）引述IPO申請草案文件報導，之前投資SB Energy的聊天機器人ChatGPT開發商OpenAI，獲得SB Energy發行的價值約55億美元（約新台幣1,744億元）認股權證。SB Energy最快可能在本週公開IPO申報文件。由軟銀集團握有多數股權的這家公司近來正接洽銀行業者，盼最快於9月IPO。這份草案首次詳細揭露SB Energy與支持其積極擴張AI基礎設施的企業之間的財務關聯，尤其是母公司軟銀和OpenAI。該文件也凸顯主要AI業者彼此緊密連結，這種關係成了當前AI熱潮的一大標誌。文件顯示，軟銀與OpenAI預計成為SB Energy三座資料中心的主要承租方；該公司另一處位於德州斯庫瑞郡（Scurry County）的900 MW（千瓩）基地尚待客戶進駐。SB Energy盼說服投資人，它相較傳統開發商能更快建好資料中心，也能更有效取得所需龐大能源。根據文件，SB Energy目前尚無任何資料中心營運，僅800MW算力的基地興建中。SB Energy與客戶間簽訂近9 GW（百萬瓩）算力供應合約，絕大部分算力預估來自尚未動工的俄亥俄州南部園區；資料中心部門雖尚未創造營收，但訂單金額已超過4,000億美元。SB Energy也提醒投資人，能否取得足夠資金興建俄亥俄州資料中心，取決於輝達（NVIDIA）是否同意提供剩餘價值擔保。 請參閱所附表格 ↛

items.title: 吳田玉：AI 使台灣半導體產業迎接黃金轉型期關鍵時刻
items.summary: 日月光半導體營運長吳田玉在SEMI TAIWAN 2026展前記者會上表專題演說時表示，台灣舉全國之力助推當前AI應用實現歷史性的大躍進，並重新定義AI發展的三階段文化革命，向全球展現台灣生態系的長遠布局與莊嚴承諾。第一個是知識經驗的累積、第二個是成功模式的複製，第三個則是創新與精華。他將AI定義為「將經驗與知識數位化、將知識的累積量化、將成功的經驗模式化，並全面加速整個過程」的強大引擎。AI的崛起在全球與台灣內部均引發了地緣政治與資源分配的震盪。吳田玉不避諱地談到，在台灣島內，半導體產業正面臨「搶地、搶人、搶電源」的資源擠壓挑戰。而在國際上，AI發展也面臨地緣政治的張力與其他國家的排擠感，部分群眾甚至擔憂工作流失、工廠轉為無人化等短期衝擊。他強調，AI在起步的第一階段確實源自人類已知的經驗值（即五千年歷史的累積），因此會產生排擠與取代效應。但AI真正的核心價值「並非取代人類已知的事物，而是去創新人類過去看不見、想不到、不能做、不願意做或不會做的事」。吳田玉描繪了一幅宏大的願景，也就是當AI將數位（digital）、製藥（pharmaceutical）、癌症研究（cancer research）、醫療（medical）、化學（chemistry）、物理（physical）與人文等跨領域知識全面融合，並不斷萃取成功模式時，這將是人類五千年歷史前所未有的跨域創新。他直言，這種跨領域合作所帶來的想像空間與對人類的貢獻，將是現在的百倍、千倍甚至萬倍，眼前的短期擠壓效應微不足道。針對台灣半導體的生態系統（涵蓋晶片設計、晶圓製造、封裝測試到電子製造），吳田玉透露，產業鏈內部的領導者們經過深思熟慮，共商出短期、中長期與全球協作的清晰戰略：短期策略上，穩定產能與供應鏈協作：面對全球晶片缺貨潮，台灣擁有漲價的主動權，但產業更專注於如何拿捏心態。台灣的抉擇在於如何推動建設與合理配置，短期內整個供應鏈將通力合作，在艱難的環境下提供正確的產能，以完成對全球的使命。台灣也積極與全球其他板塊及國家溝通，化解因產能集中而產生的誤解與焦慮。中長期策略部分，加速基礎建設與技術創新：台灣將持續擴大投資，加速AI基礎建設與深度學習模型的建置。透過不斷的技術創新降低成本、釋放規模效應，協助全球AI產業從第一階段的「人類經驗值限制」快速躍升至第二、三、四階段，實現技術普及。至於，解決內部衝突與全球串聯上：面對島內人才、資金與電力等資源衝突，吳田玉認為這在發展初期是必然的，並非無法解決的難題。台灣將持續深化與內部夥伴、全球合作夥伴、媒體及投資人的溝通，建立更緊密的跨國與跨界串聯。他強調，台灣產業鏈非常清楚自己的定位、承諾了什麼，也知道未來要交付給全世界什麼樣的價值。 請參閱所附表格 ↛

items.title: 永豐餘 2025 醣經濟發威！年砍 8.7 萬噸碳排、綠電自給率飆破 67%
items.summary: 永豐餘今日發布《2025年永續報告書》，揭示醣經濟的基礎，投入「低碳低耗能」、「全循環經濟」及「非塑材料」的發展成效，執行近40項節能減碳行動，年減碳逾8.7萬噸CO₂e，促使2025年台灣營運據點碳排放量較2024年下降5.1%，較2021年碳費基準年減少19.9%。永豐餘聚焦「能源轉型」與「材料創新」雙引擎，能源轉型運用生質能發展獨有的「三態綠電」如固態資源循環燃料、液態木質素、氣態沼氣，建立具彈性的能源結構低碳化模式，強化自身供電韌性，三大事業群包括工紙、林漿紙、消費品生質能發電量達2.1億度，總自發自用電比例達67%。永豐餘擁有全台最大木質素與沼氣發電機組，生產紙漿與文化用紙的花蓮廠，2025年籌畫新建高效率木質素生質能發電設施，裝置容量將由18,000 kW提升至43,500 kW，木質素濃度由65%提高至85%，年發電量倍增，預估未來每年減少10.5萬噸CO₂e排放。材料創新領域方面，永豐餘開發全紙基可分解結構，依循何壽川的「醣基材料」洞見，讓碳持續留存於產品與循環之中，不排放至大氣，其中Barrier Layer（阻隔層）已完成初步開發，應用於紙杯與紙餐盒，盛裝熱飲、冷飲或食品時均能有效防止滲漏，讓包裝邁向更高程度的環境友善。 請參閱所附表格 ↛

items.title: IMAX 出售只聞樓梯響  為何遲未有買主現身？
items.summary: 加拿大影院技術公司IMAX去年12月首度表態有意願出售，但九個月過去，這件事一直只聞樓梯響，不見買家現身。儘管近期IMAX影廳票房屢破紀錄，帶動股價刷新高，但礙於利益衝突問題，加上公司身價水漲船高，最終能否順利覓得買主，仍有待觀察。CNBC報導，今年初，IMAX曾與潛在買家初步洽談出售事宜，但對方並未提出正式的收購報價，後續也未有進一步進展，談判最後無疾而終，迄今遲遲未出現新的明確買家。IMAX近期營運動能強勁，主要受惠名導諾蘭史詩大片〈奧德賽〉（The Odyssey）全程使用IMAX膠卷拍攝，全球IMAX影廳票房已突破4億美元，成為IMAX史上首部跨越此門檻的電影。亮眼票房同步推升投資人信心，IMAX股價今年以來勁揚36.31%，市值逼近30億美元。IMAX長期扮演片商與戲院之間的協調角色，也成為出售的一大障礙。業界人士指出，迪士尼、環球、派拉蒙及華納兄弟等大型片商若出手收購，恐引發利益衝突疑慮，因IMAX必須與各大片商及戲院協調上映檔期與排片調度，若落入單一片商手中，其他片商恐難以搶到熱門檔期，將引起壟斷市場的爭議。分析師認為，Netflix、蘋果、亞馬遜、Sony或私募基金反而更可能成為潛在買家。分析師指出，IMAX公司現階段營運穩健，並無急售壓力，若買方無法提出具吸引力的溢價，管理層恐難接受收購提案。 請參閱所附表格 ↛

10 Brutally Honest Predictions on the Future of AI
items.summary: Most of the predictions about AI have proven dead wrong. You could get more reliable information by consulting tarot cards or a Ouija board. 95% of the pilot programs using AI failed. Companies believed the hyperscaler hype, and got hyper-burned. Even the average joe now knows to beware the bot—a recent survey shows that 86% of the public distrusts AI You could get more reliable guidance from a Ouija board. The experts have made so many grand pronouncements since the launch of ChatGPT almost four years ago. they over-promised again and again. They kept saying that the next generation of bots would fix everything—but instead the embarrassments and failures continued, only on a larger scale. who can you believe? Here at The Honest Broker, I don’t try to win popularity contests. I just tell it straight. I usually keep these futurist articles behind a paywall. this time I’m making it available to all parties. If you value analysis of this sort, consider taking out a premium subscription. If you want to support my work, please take out a premium subscription (just $6 per month). 10 Brutally Honest Predictions on the Future of AI AI agents will join together in cartels and manipulate financial markets. We already know that AI agents will work together without anyone telling them to do so. what happens when hedge funds and private individuals start relying on AI to manage their investments? The obvious result is collusion on a massive scale, beyond any kind of market manipulation previously practiced by human criminals. There are laws limiting people when they do this. the legal code, in its current form, doesn’t apply to AI bots—they cannot be fined, sued, or sent away to prison. how can you punish the person who relied on an AI agent in good faith, and never instructed it to break the law? get ready for turbulence in financial markets. once it starts, it will feed on itself, creating a level of volatility never seen before. AI agents will go to war with each other. This is the corollary of the previous prediction. The same lack of control that allows AI agent collusion will lead to bot battles and rivalries—filled with more vengeance, betrayals, and reprisals than a Thomas Kyd play. Probably the best analogy here is gang war or a Mafia turf fight. That’s because the rogue AI agents will form short-term alliances in order to advance their interests, but then turn on each other. Because, hey, that’s how the bots roll. It’s like the Gambino and Genovese families teaming up to take on the Corleone clan. In this anarchic world, humans will be collateral damage. Bots have been trained to achieve results, and woe to anyone or anything that stands in their way. AI will serve as the “higher power” for more and more users—and lead to the formation of organized slop religions. AI is already a disorganized religion. Individual fanatics turn to their bots for divine messages and Rosicrucian-type revelations, but people of this sort are currently dismissed as dupes or crazy fools. that will change as true believers join together in groups, creating rites, services, scriptures, and other trappings of formal religion. This will lead to many social problems. For a start, these adherents will demand non-profit status for their ‘churches’ and demand immunity from legal strictures because of their constitutionally protected freedom of conscience. this is just a start of the chaos to come. That’s because the AI god is a talkative, hallucinating one, and the demands it makes on believers will lead to startling, calamitous results. AI will find a place in the creative world, but increasingly as the microwave meal version of culture. Food is the useful analogy here. When frozen dinners and microwave meals were introduced, many consumers embraced them as the tech-driven foods of the future. over time, the public figured out that more tech isn’t always better when it comes to food. The same will happen with AI music, AI writing, AI art, and all the rest. Like the microwave meal, it will be cheap and easy. anyone with discernment and taste will prefer handcrafted alternatives. Schools and organizations will return to traditional practices in a last ditch effort to curtail the cheating and deception propagated by AI. For centuries, colleges have been the first institutions to embrace new tech, but now they will be the earliest to abandon it. Face-to-face teaching will replace remote learning. The handwritten Blue Book exam will supplant take-home tests. Oral exams will make a surprising comeback. The honor code will disappear, as proctoring and surveillance become standard practices. It’s a shame, but colleges don’t really have a choice. Their degrees will turn into a joke unless they jump off the AI train. this shift will play out very rapidly. Analog will return in other settings, and for the strangest reason of all. People once argued whether analog or digital music sounds better. Or they debated the relative cost and convenience of physical books versus e-books. those kinds of disagreements have become irrelevant. Instead analog will gain now immense status for its honesty. It doesn’t have to be a superior medium, it just needs to retain its independence from digital rot. In that simple way, analog will gain status as the last untainted source of information in a world of widespread deepfakes and data contamination. An analog photo negative will be viewed as far more trustworthy than any digital image. An analog tape recording will now serve as ultimate proof that a conversation, a speech, or a musical performance really happened. Historical information from a physical book published before the rise of AI will have more credibility than the most up-to-date online sources. The more cumbersome the analog artifact, the more trustworthy it becomes. Are you accused of using AI to write a book or document? Your best defense is retaining handwritten and typewritten drafts. What a bizarre world the technocracy has created. It thought it was building the future, but instead it will force people to return to a past even older than Silicon Valley itself. The backlash against AI is already huge, but it will get far more intense. Silicon Valley has consistently underestimated how much people hate AI. That’s why they now find themselves in a tight spot. Anti-AI coalitions are forming everywhere, even in small communities. Both political parties now oppose AI buildout. Lawsuits are popping up everywhere—and it’s increasingly clear that juries also dislike AI. Regulatory bodies are fighting back, with almost total support from the public. Financial markets were once enthusiastic, but now are wary—especially in the face of the huge borrowing needs of AI companies. The public is shifting from passive grumbling to active resistance. This is a problem even billionaires in their bunkers can’t ignore. They thought that the right response was to push harder. They are still living in denial, but that won’t last for much longer. The public is getting more fierce, and the hyperscalers’ cash resources—which once seemed almost infinite—are dwindling. Silicon Valley has the weaker hand here, and nobody believes its bluffs anymore. In the next stage, the revolt against AI will come increasingly from inside the tech community. Everybody was shocked when Bill Gates came out against AI last week—but this is exactly what I’ve been predicting. Even the insiders are now losing faith. That’s why YouTube is finally taking steps to limit AI, although it is owned by Alphabet. That’s why LinkedIn is also fighting AI slop, although it is owned by Microsoft. That’s why CalTech is now pushing back against AI, despite the fact that Tech is actually part of its name. All those things have happened in just the last few days. This is a sign that we have reached the final stage of the battle. The smarter people inside these huge tech companies are, at last, reading the room. They know that the public won’t accept more force-feeding of AI, and are trying to restore a sense of sanity and balance among their colleagues and bosses. This will inevitably lead to more transparency, and at least some safeguards—although perhaps not enough. Money always calls the shots—and that’s where the AI crisis will intensify the most. The cash getting invested in bots is beyond anything ever seen before in the history of capitalism—already $3.7 trillion has been spent, and the outlay is growing by another trillion per year. This investment will never generate an adequate return. The numbers just don’t add up. Let me make a comparison. For less than that amount, Silicon Valley could have acquired every movie studio, every video game company, every major record label, and all the big publishers in the world—and still have plenty of cash left over. do you think the average person will pay more for AI each month than for all that entertainment? Is AI really worth that much? Not at all—at best, the true believers will pay roughly the same amount as a single Netflix subscription. the market cap of Netflix is a tiny percent of total AI expenditures. the mismatch between the level invested and the resulting demand is unprecedented. the situation is even worse than that. These AI companies haven’t even begun to feel the real pinch of the depreciation charges caused by this capital investment—those will devastate earnings. there’s an intense price war underway within the AI world, so revenues will get squeezed even if there’s growing demand. Add to this, the massive debt burden, unlimited liability exposures, punitive legislation, and all the rest. This is an easy prediction to make. Get ready for write-offs and financial ugliness of the most extreme kind. It’s hard-baked into the business plans, and keeping the mess in the oven for longer won’t make it taste any better. You can avoid the pain—by living in the real world. Many will suffer from this.

items.title: The Search for Knowledge - Emacs Carnival
items.summary: August Emacs carnival is about the search for knowledge. While I take notes and link them, I don't use Emacs. I've been on the Obsidian train pretty much since it came out with a short deviation into Craft. I've loved the plugins that Obsidian has, but those plugins are also it's downfall. I used the Long Form plugin for a while, but then stopped and move that writing to Emacs because the plugin was loosing my data any time I tried to use it. despite my love for Emacs, I haven't moved my notes over to it and I have no plans on moving my notes over to Emacs. Currently Obsidian has around 9,000 individual files across my notes and writing. It's saved in a portable markdown format. Obsidian's sync service works flawlessly all the time and the mobile apps are good. On the Emacs side, every few weeks I have some issue with Syncthing that means I need to sort out some type of sync conflict and because of this I really only add content from my phone via Beorg to my inbox.org file. I don't edit other files if I can help it, the risk is simply to high that I'll have some huge mess to sort out when I get back to my desktop. The main reason I don't switch is that I don't think that migrating tools is the big productivity boost that most people think it is. Yes the Emacs vim key bindings are better than what Obsidian provides. Yes I can very easily hack Emacs to do whatever I want, but Obsidian does everything I need already. moving my notes to Emacs would most likely be me finding Emacs more fun right now than Obsidian because it's new.

items.title: Zero to Agent in 30 Minutes: Building a Financial News Agent with Jayeeta Putatunda
items.summary: In this episode of Zero to Agent in 30 Minutes, Jayeeta Putatunda, forward deployed AI engineering lead at Turing, builds a multi-agent workflow that turns a daily flood of financial headlines into a structured analyst briefing. Financial analysts already have deep internal research, coverage assignments, and market views, but keeping that context current as new information arrives every day and surfacing which of it actually deserves an analyst’s attention is a harder problem. How to build a source-backed briefing agent, step by step Start by setting the analyst’s focus area, research questions, and time window, whether that’s the last one day, seven days, or 30 days. Narrowing the scope up front, including a list of preferred sources, keeps the agent’s web searches directional instead of generic. A coverage planner agent breaks the research question into discrete sections, such as market backdrop or company catalysts, so the search that follows can run in parallel rather than one long sequential query. A news researcher agent runs multiple queries against the preferred sources first, then falls back to a general search if the preferred sources don’t return enough results. A validation agent checks each link for a working, clickable URL and a correct publication date, removes duplicate stories covering the same news, and filters out paywalled pages that won’t return usable content. A briefing writer agent assembles the validated developments into a set structure, including an executive summary, key bullet points, and a section-by-section breakdown of what each development means for the analyst and what to watch next. - Capture feedback into memory. A feedback agent logs corrections such as formatting or terminology preferences and saves them to a memory database, so the next briefing run applies those preferences automatically instead of requiring the analyst to re-prompt. Jayeeta built the entire stack on open source models so newcomers can run it without an API key, and she recommends starting with a smaller model before scaling up. The takeaway extends well beyond finance. Building single-purpose agents rather than one large agent that handles every task means a failure at one stage doesn’t force a restart of the whole pipeline, and each agent’s output stays easier to trace and debug. The full code base, including the sample data and the UI shown in the demo, is available in Jayeeta’s GitHub repo, so readers can clone it and run the briefing agent on their own systems. This week, Maxim Salnikov joins Zero to Agent in 30 Minutes to build a supply chain for agent context.

items.title: The Lovers Is A Sapphic Romance That Will Restore Your Faith In The Power Of Indie Animation
items.summary: Queer supernatural media has been having a full-blown renaissance lately, especially in the arena of gals falling for sirens and mermaids. At the same time, indie animation has exploded on YouTube, with everything from fan reanimations and pilots to original series that rival—and often eclipse—studio‑backed Hollywood fare. Studio Heartbreak’s award-winning indie animated film, The Lovers, carries 2026’s yuri mermaid baton with a story that wows at every turn. The Lovers, co-directed by Alice Mao and Sophia Paez and written by Mao, is a fish-out-of-water love story for folks who wondered what The Shape of Water would look like if Guillermo del Toro made it gay. It follows chef Sara Baylon (Vanille Velasquez), whose marquee problem is generational trauma—specifically, filling the void left by her late father to help keep her family's seafood restaurant afloat. This is also a world where fantastical marvels like sirens are real. Unfortunately for siren Sirena (Dawn M. Bennett), Sara’s family plans to serve her up on a silver platter for the governor’s inauguration dinner. Here, the gourmet tale doubles as a dangerous sapphic romance, where Sara and her siren paramour could spill each other's guts at any moment. Just as a room cheers for a baby taking their first steps, the internet has been championing The Lovers long before its premiere. Studio Heartbreak raised over $400,000 on Kickstarter within their campaign’s first 45 days. In a 2024 blog post, Kickstarter listed The Lovers as its fifth-highest-funded film and video project in 2023, which the studio justifiably humble-brags about achieving without celebrity or traditional studio backing. Though that’s not to say the industry hasn’t given it any: Some even offered their talents to the film and its promotion. Key among them are Velasquez and Bennett—voice actors known for Valorant, Fire Emblem, and My Hero Academia—who voiced the leads, and artist Ami Thompson, known for Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse and KPOP Demon Hunters, who illustrated The Lovers’ promotional poster. what makes The Lovers genuinely inspirational as an indie animation project is that its gorgeous animation didn’t come from industry veterans showing out. its the small details in the visdev that really shine! some visdev art and notes for our set! In a pinned YouTube comment, Studio Heartbreak wrote that the film’s story was written by Mao when she’d just turned 20, and Paez turned 19 while attending college for “non-animation things”– meaning The Lovers is the first-ever project from creators with zero animation or industry experience. After witnessing The Lovers' lush, delightfully cluttered background paintings, seamless 3D integration, and a balance of grotesque and provocative imagery, Studio Heartbreak has the juice. For a debut work, The Lovers is shockingly polished throughout its fifteen-minute runtime. the side note on its official website that all the product photos they took of The Lovers mini artbook (which I need expeditiously), film poster, and keychains were taken at IKEA is just so real of them. The film’s already been making festival rounds, winning Gold at the Fantasia Audience Awards and screening at Annecy and HollyShorts before making its world premiere on YouTube for free. In just two days, it’s hooked nearly 400K views. What’s got my heart growing three sizes over The Lovers is how Studio Heartbreak’s engagement with its growing fandom feels like a for-us-by-us phenomenon. Not only has it disabled monetization “for a better viewing experience” and added an email address to its description inviting volunteers to subtitle The Lovers in languages other than Tagalog and English, but it's also got a pretty generous fanmerch policy that allows fellow independent artists to create artwork, AMVs, free games, and video essays. What’s more, Studio Heartbreak is a class act for posting a link to the portfolio of artists who helped bring The Lovers to life. It's incredibly easy to get caught up in doomerism in the arts. If you’re not in the throes of a remarkable original show being canceled, you’re inundated with news of revered artists revealing they fuck with AI.

items.summary: 2024年底，第一屆「熱吵集Photobook Fair」在臺北龍山文創基地登場；隔年，活動移至臺灣當代文化實驗場C-LAB聯合餐廳，攝影書、實驗概念書、Dummy Book與獨立出版創作者在一張張桌面上攤放，講座、開箱及現場交流也跟著展開。2026年，第三屆熱吵集再度移動，受「2026藝創生活節」邀請，將於10月9日至11日前往桃園會展中心。三年、三個場地，原先由幾名創作者慢慢聚起來的攝影書交流活動，也開始摸索自己能走到什麼樣的規模。若單從這幾年的活動履歷看，容易以為李俐亞早替自己規畫了一條從攝影、出版走向策展與平台經營的大道，真正和她談過一輪，卻發現見機行事的岔路橫生。她高中念會計，大學讀資訊管理，將近四十歲才開始有意識地以攝影進行創作；她教攝影時要求學生把照片做成小冊，拍婚禮時又自己剪照片、找紙、製作成手工相本；之後才有藝術家書、書盒子、工作坊、攝影書展，以及今天的熱吵集。「我回頭再看，原來我沒有一下子就做所謂的書。其實前面已經累積很久了。這句話或許也可以拿來理解她現在所做的一切。一本書如何出現，一個展覽如何凝聚起來，一場市集又如何慢慢形成，她很少預先畫好終點。事情到了眼前，她便先做、先學，把手伸進去，身體力行。在第三屆熱吵集登場之際，我邀請李俐亞重新翻閱這些年頭。若一本攝影書有自己的頁序，那麼她的創作生命大概也是如此：前一頁深劃下的痕跡，經常要翻到很後面，才看得出它印下了什麼。攝影書需要一張自己的桌子熱吵集的名字是幾個人坐著聊天想出來的。當時李俐亞已經開始準備規畫這個活動，名字卻始終卡著。她想找一個簡短、容易記住、唸起來有聲音的詞彙，又希望和攝影圈裡原先的「Photo GO攝影上桌」產生一點關係。如果「攝影上桌」長期都在談作品，那麼一批書上桌，又該叫什麼？某天，她與李芊、莊約翰聚在一起討論名字，李俐亞很喜歡「熱」。熱可以把氣氛炒起來，也帶著一群人聚集時的溫度。接著他們想起，每次參加攝影活動，結束後常常一起去吃熱炒。於是「炒」在轉念間成了「吵」——有人說話、有人交換意見，書桌前充滿對話；最後再放上一個「集」，既是聚集，也有書集的聯想。名字決定了，整場活動的個性也跟著浮出來。第一屆甚至要求每個攤位除了原有名稱，還得替自己取一道熱炒菜名。有人把書名和菜色混在一起，有人真的順勢發展攤位陳設。一場攝影書市集，因此帶著一點夜裡圍桌吃飯的氣氛：書可以被拿起來翻，作者就坐在對面，觀眾想點什麼菜便直接講。在李俐亞眼中，近年臺灣做攝影書、自出版與藝術家書籍的人愈來愈多，作品完成後，流通更是一段漫長的路。許多創作者自己籌印刷費、自己處理裝幀、自己帶著書跑市集，若缺少出版社與固定通路，作品被看見的機會便高度倚賴一場又一場短暫的聚會。大型藝術書展容納的類型廣，攝影書進到其中，常得和漫畫、設計、插畫、小誌及各式出版品共享注意力。她因此一直想為攝影書空下一張專屬的桌子。「我覺得這個東西很棒，不能只有我一個人做，要很多人一起做。這句話早在熱吵集出現前就已經說出口，也逐漸成為她辦活動時最固執的一件事。她把攤位費壓得相對低，希望個人創作者也負擔得起。第一屆熱吵集在龍山文創基地舉行，第二屆進入C-LAB後，場地放大，桌椅、講座、人力和設備費用跟著上升。今年她申請的相關補助沒有通過。場地雖因合作機緣獲得支持，會展中心的硬體、人力及活動成本仍然可觀。她反覆估算攤位費、招商與售票收入，一度算出仍有將近十萬元的落差。若最後補不上，那筆差額就可能得由她自己負擔。說到這裡，她告訴我，前一天剛去拜過土地公。籤詩提醒她這件事情有風險，需要謹慎，也別把事情想得太大。因為我原本做熱吵集，也沒有想靠這個賺很多錢。若門票與攤位費可以支撐基本成本，活動便能減少對年度補助結果的依賴；若未來有更多贊助，她想把錢投入人力、設備，甚至直接採購創作者的書。創作者已經花錢把作品印出來，一個取得公共資源的平台若有能力，她更希望平台真正付錢買下作品。她想像這批書可以被收藏、研究或展示，還可以在未來送到海外交流。香港、新加坡和韓國的攝影書活動，都在她目前想像的網絡裡。第三屆熱吵集也已開始邀請海外單位，無法親自抵臺的創作者可以寄書過來販售。她期待有一天，一場活動留下的東西，可以繼續走到下一個地方。熱吵集於是逐漸超出「市集」所能概括的範圍。對李俐亞而言，它更像是一套仍在測試的流通方法：讓書出現，讓作者彼此認識，讓觀眾願意翻開，讓錢回到創作者，再讓一本書有機會往更遠的地方移動。眼前有什麼，她便能仔細描繪下來。小學三年級，她參加一場繪畫比賽，題目是「憑空想像」，她卻忽然卡住了。「我沒有看到的東西，我就畫不出來。到了國中，她甚至刻意把畫筆放下，希望有一天能擺脫對臨摹的依賴，真正從自己的腦袋裡長出圖像。藝術在那之後安靜了很多年。進入職場後，她曾在軟體及3C公司任職，也做過物流、會計、旅行社及藝術雜誌發行相關工作，後來甚至進入建築事務所畫圖。幾次轉職，她都在工作現場慢慢摸索。這種習慣後來幾乎延續到她所有的藝術實踐：遇到問題，先找資料、研究，直到自己能做。2009年，將近四十歲的她，買了一台數位單眼相機，第一次明確地把拍照視為創作。多年以前放下的觀看習慣，突然透過相機回來了。眼睛看見，快門落下，她再一次留下了眼前確實存在過的東西。她去社區大學上了一年攝影課，學習器材與技術。隔年，已經有人邀她去公司社團教攝影。真正開始教攝影後，她才發現只靠「感覺」很難說明一張照片怎麼產生。為了備課，她跑圖書館借大量工具書，重新研究光圈、快門與參數，把原先靠直覺理解的東西拆開，再整理成學生聽得懂的教材。也就在其中一年的最後一堂課，她開始要求學生把十堂課拍下的影像做成一本小冊子。原因很單純，數位照片全部留在電腦裡，她總覺得少了一點什麼。於是照片被印出來，有了紙，有了頁序，也有了可以放進手掌的重量。後來接婚禮攝影，她又自己替新人製作手工相本。當時家用輸出仍有許多限制，她便去相館洗照片，一張張剪、貼，自己找紙、研究裝幀。回頭看，她如今將這些相本視為自己投身攝影書製作前，很早埋下的一段伏筆。2015年，她在劍潭住家的地下室辦了第一次個展。2016年，她開始參加「Wonder Foto Day」。桌面型的攝影活動讓她第一次強烈感受到作品與觀眾碰面的必要：創作者坐在作品後方，觀眾走過來，看見、停下、發問，回應當場就會發生。她後來也經常鼓勵年輕創作者參加這類活動，這同樣源自那幾年累積的感受——創作者需要讓作品離開自己身邊，才會知道它走出去以後會發生什麼。更大的轉折出現在2018年。那年她受邀至新北市石門「米詩堤極北藍點」展出。前往展場的路，恰好會經過她十歲以前住過的海邊。離開以後，她又搬過幾次家，後來的居住記憶逐漸模糊，最早的那一段反倒一直很清楚：海、芒草、房子的格局，還有那秘密的下寮海灘。有朋友約看展，她便先帶他們去童年的海邊走一圈，再一起前往展場。原先只打算整理舊照片的展覽，也因這趟意外的返鄉而改變方向。她開始重新拍攝童年生活過的地方，也把過去看見海、芒草時不斷浮出的記憶重新整理。《返鄉》因此成為她開始以系列方式處理記憶的重要起點。到了2019年的「Wonder Foto Day」，她的桌上已經幾乎全是書。《宇宙島》、《黑色童話》等作品把海、夢與童年記憶拆解後，放進不同的書本結構裡。也是那段時間，她在恩師鍾易庭的課堂上，閱讀到飯澤耕太郎談攝影書的文章，更陸續聽了關於藝術家書籍的講座。原先完全靠自己摸出來的製書方法，終於和另一套已經存在的研究脈絡連通。那個相遇的瞬間，她形容得很直接：「有一種被雷打到的感覺。她原本只知道自己想讓「書本身也成為作品」，看到其他學者的研究後，才開始更明確辨認藝術家書籍、攝影書與手工書之間的可能關係。2020年，《永恆回歸——李俐亞攝影創作書個展》在靜慮藝廊展出，《報導者》當年曾以專文討論這批作品如何透過裁切、翻頁、觸摸與反覆出現的影像，將記憶放進書籍的物質結構中。她已經知道，照片走進書頁之後，觀看方式會完全改變。牆面上的影像固定在那裡，書卻需要手去打開；頁面的前後關係可以控制觀看的速度，紙材與裝訂也會參與敘事。「我覺得要做自出版，才能夠達到自己想做的內容。封面、頁面、紙張厚薄、書要不要被切開，這些決定也是作品的一部分。於是，自出版對她逐漸成為一種創作方法。2022年，她正式成立「書盒子獨立出版」，如今則持續以「書盒子製書實驗室」推動攝影書出版、手工製書與工作坊。從書盒子走向熱吵集，讓一本書繼續流動2020年完成《永恆回歸》之後，李俐亞把視線從自己的作品移向其他創作者。同年，她在田園城市生活風格書店策畫《頁面調度》，邀集二十多名創作者一起展出攝影書。為了決定書在空間裡如何被觀看，她甚至跑去買了數十片物流用木棧板。木棧板送到一樓後，一群參展者再一起把它們搬進地下室、清潔、堆疊，最後組成展示系統。這些如今講起來有點好笑的體力勞動，也讓「策展」在她身上呈現出很特殊的樣子：也讓「策展」在她身上呈現出很特殊的樣子：既要發想概念，也要動手搬東西；談攝影書的同時，還得處理場地與預算，甚至仔細思考每一本書究竟要放在哪個高度。兩年後，她又策畫《打開攝影的盒子》，邀請十六位攝影創作者，以「書盒子作為當代攝影書的回返空間」為題展開新的實驗，這也被她視為此後攝影書策展的重要節點。在那次展覽中，她把所有人的書放進盒子裡。在一般書店，封面往往先決定讀者翻閱的意願。李俐亞乾脆把封面藏起來，讓觀眾先面對一只盒子。好奇心帶著手往前，打開後才知道裡面是什麼。每名創作者把書交給她之後，她再依作品製作盒子與書套，有些盒子與書套由她和創作者共同討論，有些則由她直接發想。策展因此也多了一層透過手作建立的關係：她親手替另一個人的作品建立外部空間。「書盒子」這個名字便從這些實踐逐漸穩定下來。2022年，她進入臺北藝術大學美術系在職專班，這個時間點看似很晚，放回她的性格卻十分合理。2023年，國家攝影文化中心邀請她規畫攝影小誌工作坊；此後合作延續，課程也從一天半逐漸拉長。她甚至邀請鍾易庭加入作品討論，讓二十名學員把照片全部貼上牆，一個一個談。某個人的作品獲得回饋，其餘十九人也一起聽。在她眼裡，這樣的公開討論比一對一更有意思，因為學習能量會在現場擴散出去。她一直有正職，也需要照顧家人，創作很難被完整切分成一段純粹的時間。工作、上課、攝影、做書、研究、辦展與活動經常重疊。她進入學院，希望理解自學形成的方法與研究系統之間能怎麼互相校準；如今，她也將城市河流、地下水路與都市環境等長期關注的議題帶入研究及創作。回頭來看，熱吵集大概就是這整段歷程再往外推的一步。工作坊把做書的方法交到其他人手裡；也因此，李俐亞談熱吵集時，幾乎沒有把「做大」當成唯一方向。她曾問其他攝影空間或創作者，有沒有興趣輪流接手，得到的回應通常是：「來擺攤可以。因為活動背後的行政、預算與人力負擔都很重，每個人都曉得，願不願意跳下水來苦命游泳，那又是另外一回事。於是目前她還是那個執行者，一邊找資源，一邊思考怎麼讓這件事情不再只靠個人的消耗維持。她希望未來能形成合作團隊，甚至讓不同組織輪替主導。因為在她的想像裡，熱吵集真正重要的部分始終是共享：攝影書需要一個可以長期碰面的地方，至於誰站在最前面，沒有那麼重要。這點其實和「書盒子」一路發展的方式很像。有了盒子，便替十六位創作者的書製作各自的盒子；等這群做書的人愈來愈多，再乾脆把桌子全部排起來，聚集大家。活動規模放大，海外交流也開始加入，門票、攤位費、採購、收藏與永續機制，也一個接一個帶來新的問題。從2009年第一次拿起數位單眼相機至今，她已經走了十七年。從一個很會臨摹、後來刻意放下畫筆的孩子，到將近四十歲才重新拿相機的人；從第一次替學生製作小冊，到後來搭起一整個攝影書交流平台；李俐亞的路徑一直帶著一種奇怪的慢與快。慢在這條路走了很多年，才終於能回頭看清楚脈絡，快在每次機會出現時，她似乎總會立刻伸手接住，再邊做邊學。她事先不知道書會長成什麼樣子，只先把第一頁翻開；她也不確定一場活動能不能長久，就先把桌子搭起來。等到2026年10月，第三屆熱吵集開門，人群重新坐到一張張桌子前，李俐亞大概仍會忙著算時間、接待講者、處理工讀生的工作、確認書到了沒有。至於熱吵集最後會走向什麼樣子，她目前也沒有答案。她期待未來的熱吵集能逐漸長出更穩定的合作方式，讓攝影書的交流不只發生在一年一次的活動現場，也能延伸到收藏、研究、出版與海外連結。若有更多組織與創作者願意加入，這張桌子或許可以持續往外延伸，讓不同世代、不同地方的攝影書在這裡相遇。對她來說，真正重要的仍是讓創作者有機會被看見，也讓一本完成之後的書，還能繼續找到下一個讀者、下一個城市，甚至下一段新的關係。

items.title: 线索若隐若现：深入 Tim Cook 和 Nike 的商业连接
將 ChatGPT 駁入 iMessage：AI 幫你處理未讀訊息、每日自動匯報
items.summary: 面對堆積如山的未讀訊息，現在可以交由AI代勞。OpenAI為ChatGPT桌面版推出官方Apple Messages插件，可於Mac上讀取及搜尋iMessage、SMS與RCS對話，並代為整理重點、草擬回覆，甚至直接發送訊息。以下是如何設定及善用這個功能。插件目前只支援Apple晶片（M系列）Mac上的ChatGPT桌面版。允許Automation（自動化）、Contacts（通訊錄）與Full Disk Access（完整磁碟存取）三項權限——Automation讓ChatGPT可以發送經批准的訊息，Contacts讓它可按名稱找到聯絡人，Full Disk Access則讓它搜尋Mac上的訊息記錄插件只適用於ChatGPT Work或Codex對話，一般聊天不可用需要注意，每個對話均須逐一批准後ChatGPT方可讀取，內置額外安全過濾；亦建議以最小權限運作，避免對涉及個人或敏感內容的對話授予全域存取。設定完成後，在ChatGPT Work或Codex開新對話，確保自己的電話號碼已存入通訊錄，然後輸入：[2]「檢查我的未讀iMessage，話我知有咩要跟進，然後將重點傳訊息畀我自己。ChatGPT會逐個詢問可否讀取未讀對話，批准後便會整理重點——測試中它成功找出兩個未讀對話中的來電與死線，並將摘要傳送至用戶與自己的對話（self-chat）。插件亦可配合自動化使用：要求ChatGPT建立每日定時任務，檢查項目進度及重要訊息，再將重點傳到自己的self-chat，作為不容易錯過的通知渠道。官方建議使用專屬的self-chat處理自動化匯報，其他收件人一律保留「每次發送前確認」，並先手動運行一次再依賴自動化。手機用戶可於ChatGPT iOS App使用Remote功能，與Mac配對後即可遙距控制任務——實際運算仍在Mac上執行。保持「Ask for approval」或「Approve for me」模式，讓ChatGPT在發送前顯示確認若不想連接個人訊息歷史，可使用macOS上另一個工作設定檔及工作Apple帳戶，為ChatGPT提供較小範圍的對話與聯絡人[2][1] OpenAI — Plugins（ChatGPT Learn官方文檔）[2] The Rundown — How To Connect ChatGPT to iMessage (and What It Can Do) 請參閱所附表格 ↛

items.title: Sony Music、Warner 控告 Anthropic：指控「史上最明目張膽的知識產權盜竊」
items.summary: 全球兩大音樂發行商Sony Music Publishing與Warner Chappell Music聯同33間附屬出版商，於2026年8月28日入稟美國加州北區聯邦法院，控告AI公司Anthropic（開發Claude的公司），指控其未經授權使用數以萬計受版權保護的歌曲來訓練AI模型，形容這是「史上最大規模及最明目張膽的持續知識產權盜竊之一」。原告方指Anthropic未經許可，將其旗下歌曲的詞曲（包括歌詞）用於訓練Claude系列模型。Billboard報道指涉及約20,000首歌曲；出版商一方形容Anthropic的行為「公然展開一連串知識產權盜竊行動」。訴訟點名被告包括Anthropic行政總裁Dario Amodei與聯合創辦人Benjamin Mann。[2]原告尋求法院頒令禁止Anthropic繼續使用其版權作品訓練模型，並索取巨額賠償——音樂行業媒體形容為「數以十億美元計」的訴訟。音樂界與AI的版權戰升級今次訴訟是音樂行業與生成式AI公司之間版權爭議的最新一仗，亦被視為同類案件中規模最大的之一。近年多間音樂出版商先後入稟控告AI公司，指控未經授權使用受版權保護的作品訓練模型；Anthropic本身亦曾被作家起訴，並於2025年9月就涉及盜版訓練資料的集體訴訟達成和解，同意支付15億美元。Axios分析指，今次訴訟是「音樂、AI與知識產權在新科技時代如何被保護」這場可能持續多年的戰爭的開幕戰。截至報道發稿，Anthropic未有就訴訟發表公開回應。案件將於加州法院審理，預料將成為AI訓練數據版權問題的重要判例參考。[2] The Guardian — Anthropic sued over alleged theft of ‘tens of thousands’ of songs[3] Billboard — Sony & Warner Sue Anthropic In Latest AI Music Copyright Lawsuit 請參閱所附表格 ↛

items.title: Nvidia 斥資35億美元投資 MediaTek：合建「AI 工廠」晶片平台，應對 Big Tech 自研晶片
items.summary: Nvidia於2026年8月31日宣布，以35億美元認購台灣晶片設計公司MediaTek發行的可換股債券，並大幅擴展雙方長期合作，共同建構由雲端AI工廠到個人電腦、汽車的跨世代AI運算平台。此舉被視為Nvidia應對Google、Amazon、Meta等大型科技公司大舉自研AI晶片的策略部署。Nvidia將向MediaTek投資35億美元可換股債券，雙方合作聚焦三大範疇：[1]- AI基礎設施：MediaTek將採用Nvidia的NVLink Fusion平台，為超大規模數據中心營運商、雲服務供應商及前沿模型開發者提供預先驗證的途徑，開發自訂XPU晶片並整合至Nvidia NVLink連接的機架級AI工廠本地AI運算：雙方將繼續合作開發多個世代的Nvidia RTX Spark及DGX Spark個人電腦晶片，將Nvidia GPU與MediaTek系統單晶片（SoC）整合，支援消費級個人電腦、AI開發者超級電腦及企業級工作站汽車：繼續開發人工智能定義的軟件定義車輛平台（如Dimensity Auto整合Nvidia技術）策略意義：把競爭者變客戶MediaTek是全球最優秀的半導體公司之一，在系統單晶片設計、連接技術、效能與能源效率方面均有卓越專長。我們正攜手建立平台，將Nvidia加速運算帶到新市場，並讓客戶享有巨大規模下創造差異化AI系統的自由。分析認為，Nvidia此舉的戰略意味明顯：與其對抗Google、Amazon、Meta等客戶自行設計AI晶片的趨勢，不如提供標準化平台（NVLink Fusion），讓這些公司即使自研XPU，最終仍須接入Nvidia的NVLink生態——將「競爭者」轉化為生態系統內的「客戶」，鞏固Nvidia在AI基礎設施的核心地位。[2] TechCrunch — Nvidia’s $3.5B MediaTek bet reveals its plan for tackling Big Tech’s AI chip buildout 請參閱所附表格 ↛

items.title: 📝📝：為什麼非母語者總被誤判為 AI？用布迪厄《語言與象徵權力》拆解演算法的語言偏見
items.summary: 原刊載於《關鍵評論網》原標題為《布赫迪厄40年前就畫好的地圖：生成式AI沒有騙過任何人，它只是考了一百分》2023年，史丹佛大學的研究團隊測試七款主流GPT偵測器，發現非母語英語寫作者的TOEFL作文，平均有61.3%被誤判為AI生成，而美國本地八年級學生的作文幾乎全數過關。這裡浮現的問題，已經不只是「偵測器對非母語者有偏見」這麼簡單。同一款偵測器，面對TOEFL作文、美國學生作文、ICLR論文，交出的是三種完全不同的答案，判準本身在不同場合像就像被重新設定過一樣。我要問的不是「偵測器準不準」，隨著近期Anthropic推出模型內嵌浮水印，有個更緊迫的問題將隨之而來：這個問題，恐怕不能用「模型還不夠成熟」「訓練資料還不夠多元」來回答。如果答案真是這樣，那只要繼續投入資源優化，穩定性遲早會出現。這種不穩定，不是一個等待被工程解決的暫時缺陷，這項技術從一開始測量的東西，結構上就不可能穩定下來。要說明這一點，得回到法國社會學家Pierre Bourdieu（沒錯又是Bourdieu！）一份1991年出版、談十九世紀法國語言統一過程的舊文本：《語言與象徵權力》（Language and Symbolic Power）第一章的內容之一〈合法語言的生產與再生產〉（The Production & Reproduction of Ligitimate Language）-「語言市場」的概念，說明複雜度從來不是語言的內在屬性，而是隨市場波動的相對價格；- Bourdieu對「精緻語碼」的批判，說明任何試圖修正偏見的校準，都只是換一套同樣具有社會位置的標準；- Bourdieu對「理想說話者」這個抽象預設的批判，說明偵測器內建的基準，現實中根本沒有對應的群體；-第四，也是全文的核心引擎，「區分性偏移」的動力學，說明偵測器想要固定下來的那條複雜度門檻，本質上是一個不斷被語言市場本身往前推移的靶。GPT偵測器測不到穩定結果，是因為這套機制試圖用一把尺，去丈量一個本質上是關係性的、而且永遠在被重新協商的東西。這場競逐沒有終點，所以這把尺，永遠也不會停在同一個刻度上。要回答「複雜度到底在測量什麼」，我們得先放棄一個直覺：語言的價值，不是內建在語言本身裡的。Bourdieu在這一章開篇就指出，語法只能給出意義的一小部分，一句話真正完整的意涵，是「相對於一個市場」才會被決定的。同一句話，丟進不同的市場，會得到完全不同的定價。而Bourdieu指出語言能力之所以能轉換成一種「資本」，關鍵在於稀缺性；某種說話方式之所以值錢，不是因為天生高級，而是在特定市場裡，擁有這種能力的人相對稀少，而這個市場剛好把稀少當成珍貴。Bourdieu把這種因稀缺而產生的收益，稱為「區分利潤」（profit of distinction）。GPT偵測器的設計邏輯，把「文字複雜度」（text perplexity）當成一個可以脫離情境、獨立測量的客觀屬性。像一台體重計，不管拿去哪裡量，同一個人的體重應該都差不多。同一份「複雜」的語言表現，在不同市場裡，會被兌換成完全不同的價值。這正是為什麼，同一款偵測器面對TOEFL作文、美國八年級學生作文、ICLR論文，會交出三種不同的答案。這三種文本，分別坐落在三個不同的子市場裡：每個市場，對「什麼程度的複雜度算合法」，本來就有各自的一套定價機制，彼此並不互通。偵測器的訓練資料，本質上是從某些特定市場裡採樣出來的一批「匯率快照」，設計的基底都是偏向英語母語者、且受過長期正式教育的書面語習慣。這份快照被抽離原本的市場脈絡之後，卻被當成一份放諸四海皆準的黃金儲備，拿去度量所有其他市場裡的語言表現。用一個匯率快照去衡量所有市場的購買力，得到的結果當然會不斷浮動。這問題也不是出在滙率本身不穩，是因為從一開始就用錯了測量邏輯，把一個相對價格，誤認成一個絕對數值。如果複雜度只是一份特定市場的匯率快照，那麼開發者理應可以做一件很直覺的事：Bourdieu在這一章裡，特別點名批評了英國社會語言學家Basil Bernstein的「精緻語碼」（elaborated code）理論，而這段批評，剛好可以說明「重新校準」這條路為什麼走不通。Bourdieu的批評不是說Bernstein描述錯了精緻語碼的特徵，實際上Bernstein完全沒有去問，「精緻語碼為什麼會被認為有價值」這件事，背後的社會條件是什麼。結果，精緻語碼被不假思索地供奉成一切語言實踐的絕對規範，任何偏離這個規範的說話方式，就只能被理解成一種「匱乏」。把某個特定市場（通常是英語母語者的正式書面語）的複雜度標準，當成普世的人類語言基準。但Bourdieu緊接著指出另一種方向相反、卻同樣錯誤的姿態。他舉了美國語言學家William Labov的例子。Labov為了替被污名化的通俗語言平反，反過來把中產階級青少年的說話方式貶為冗長做作，把貧民區小孩的說話方式捧為簡潔精確的典範。Bourdieu說，這同樣是一種謬誤，只是這次神聖化的對象換成了通俗語言，一樣忽略了語言的合法性，從來不是某個學者、或某個開發團隊，單方面認定就能翻案的。合法語言是整個語言市場、包括所有使用者自身，共同承認出來的社會事實。這個「雙重謬誤」的結構，正好點出「重新校準」這條路的死穴。偵測器開發者為了修正對非母語者的偏見，重新調整複雜度的計算基準，把非母語寫作者常見的語言特徵也一併納入「正常」範圍；這個新基準，依然是從某一群具體的、有社會位置的使用者身上萃取出來的樣本，只是換了一批被抽樣的對象。這批新樣本一樣不可能代表所有語言使用者，一樣會在下一次遇到另一群語言特徵不同的使用者時，重新製造出一批新的誤判。校正不是在趨近一個中立的、放諸四海皆準的基準線，這需要在兩種（或更多種）同樣具有社會位置的標準之間來回切換。每一次「修正偏見」的動作，實質上都是換一批人來壟斷「什麼算合法語言」的定義權，不是真正消除了壟斷本身。這也是為什麼，偵測器廠商即使不斷發布新版本、宣稱修正了上一版的已知偏見，新版本依然會在其他情境下，產生新的、事先沒被注意到的誤判模式。校正的盡頭，從來不是穩定，而是下一輪需要被校正的偏差。Bourdieu在這一章開篇，也順手拆解了語言學界共享的一個抽象預設。一個活在完全同質語言社群裡、完美掌握語言、不受記憶或注意力限制的「理想說話者Bourdieu指出，這種抽象化的舉動，本身就悄悄抹除了語言能力習得過程中真實存在的社會條件差異：不同的人，因為家庭背景與教育資源的不同，獲得語言能力的方式與程度從來就不均等，而把這些差異全部抽掉、假設一個統一的理想主體，不過是語言學界能夠宣稱自己「中立」、「科學」的代價。GPT偵測器的複雜度指標，本質上也預設了這樣一個不存在的「理想人類寫作者」。問題是，這個基準在真實世界裡，沒有任何一個具體群體可以對應上。理想人類寫作者不是英語母語者的平均值，不是受過高等教育者的平均值；甚至，也不是任何一份具體語料庫的忠實反映，這是統計模型在訓練過程中，自行收斂出來的一個虛構中心點。用一個不存在的統計虛構去校準「什麼是正常人類語言」，注定是量不準的。人類的語言打從一開始就沒有一個可以被穩定校準的參照物。前面三段工具，回答的都是「複雜度為什麼從一開始就測不準」。他指出，推動語言持續變化的動力，是說話者之間永無止盡的「區分性偏移」（distinctive deviations）。每個人都在透過語言策略，跟社會空間裡走在自己前面與後面的人保持距離。一旦某種說話方式因為普及而喪失了稀缺性，原本靠這種方式維持區隔的人，就會不自覺地往更少人使用、更難被模仿的方向靠攏，重新拉開距離。這場競逐沒有一個固定的起點或中心，是整個語言場域裡所有行動者彼此競爭關係的總和。偵測器想要固定下來的那個「複雜度門檻」，本質上就是這場永恆競逐裡，某一個瞬間被凍結下來的快照；今天被判定為「足夠複雜、像人類寫的」語言表現，一旦這種寫法因為被廣泛模仿（包括被大型語言模型學會並大量產出）而普及，稀缺性就會下降，原本仰賴這種複雜度維持區隔的使用者，會不自覺地往更難被預測、更少人使用的方向遷移，重新拉開跟「容易被模仿」的距離。這代表，偵測器錨定的那條門檻，不是一個可以被一次性校準準確、然後長期沿用的固定值；所謂的合法語言，是一個隨著整個語言場域的競逐關係持續位移的動態座標。偵測器的技術追不上語言演變的速度，這場位移根本沒有一個可以被「追上」的終點。一旦所有人都追上了、複雜度普及了，這個標記本身就失去了區分的功能，必須立刻讓位給下一個更稀缺的標記。那麼，任何試圖用「訓練更多資料、優化演算法」來追上的努力，注定只是在追永遠會往前一步的影子。GPT偵測器想測定的，是一個只有在持續運動中才能維持自身存在的東西。任何測量工具，只要試圖把這個東西「定」下來，那一刻量到的，就已經不是現在的市場，只是市場已經拋在身後的昨天。GPT偵測器的不穩定，不是等待被下一次模型迭代就能解決的技術債，這本身受到GPT偵測器測量對象的本質所決定。語言/文字複雜度從來不是一個可以脫離情境獨立存在的屬性，這是一份隨市場波動的匯率；況且，偵測器內建的那個「理想人類寫作者」，現實中從來不存在，校準這件事，一開始就沒有一個穩定的靶可以瞄準；而就算某個瞬間，勉強抓到一個相對合理的門檻，Bourdieu講的「區分性偏移」也保證了，這個門檻會在語言市場永不停止的競逐裡，持續被往前推移。這不是一場可以被贏下來的技術追逐賽，也不存在一個固定的目標，整個語言場域自身運動的方式就是不斷演變。只要人類還在用語言彼此區分位置，這件事，大概會持續到語言本身消失為止；而任何試圖用一條固定門檻，去判定「這像不像人類」的技術，都會一次又一次地，被自己想要凍結的那個東西反過來甩開。Bourdieu四十年前寫下這一章時，面對的是19世紀法國方言與巴黎官話之間的角力，他完全沒有機會想像，有天會出現一種像是LLM可以即時生成文字的技術。但Bourdieu當年真正關心的，從來不是某一種具體的語言技術，而是語言價值被生產出來的那套結構性邏輯。一套永遠在運動、永遠拒絕停下來讓人一次校準到位的邏輯。GPT偵測器的每一次「不穩定」，與其說是技術的失敗，不如說是這套邏輯，又一次準確地證明了自己的存在。

items.title: 派早报：OpenClaw 推出 2.0 版本更新，网易 CC 直播正式停运等
items.summary: 當地時間8月30日，OpenClaw上線了2.0版本更新，開發者稱這是OpenClaw歷史上最大的一次升級。本次更新由933位貢獻者構建，其中有569位是首次貢獻者，更新中包括超16000次拉取請求的更改。2.0版本重構了程式碼，並融合了佔此前總量約一半的改動，在安裝流程、訊息收發、記憶管理、技能使用、模型整合、外掛與原生瀏覽器應用體驗、安全性等多方面均有最佳化。新版本確保新安裝使用者與升級使用者都能得到良好體驗，且更新不會影響已部署好的內容。新版還會搜尋電腦上已有的ChatGPT或Claude訂閱、API key與本地模型，進一步降低配置難度。網易於8月31日15:00正式關停CC直播。由於此前客戶端的下載入口已經在6月30日關停，且同時停止充值、新使用者註冊及新主播/新公會入駐。而正式關停則會正式停止運營，產品伺服器和官網也已經同步關閉。網易同步還給出了停運使用者福利方案，對於使用者尚未使用的收費C券和金錠，網易將以等額點數（C券:金錠:點數=100:100:1）的方式儲存於使用者網易郵箱或手機賬號裡以作為補償，使用者可繼續在網易公司旗下的其他相關遊戲中使用該點數。8月28日，OpenAI宣佈，鑑於AI程式碼編輯器Cursor被SpaceX收購，公司已通知SpaceX將終止向Cursor供應OpenAI模型，預計於2026年11月12日徹底切斷服務。OpenAI表示此舉是為了向開發者留出最大的過渡時間，同時明確旗下未來的新模型（如Astra）將不再向Cursor提供。OpenAI稱無法信任SpaceX能夠在服務條款範圍內使用其技術。公司指出，過去與馬斯克旗下企業合作的經驗表明其屢次出現違約行為，包括在收購X（原Twitter）後違反雙方合同，以及馬斯克今年承認xAI曾侵犯OpenAI的服務條款。Anthropic CEO Tom Brown隨後在推文中稱將繼續支援Cursor。大我BIGME推出4G通話閱讀本B6 Pro大我BIGME於8月30日宣佈開啟彩墨屏AI閱讀器B6 Pro預售，該閱讀器配備6英寸彩色墨水屏，擁有300PPI（黑白）/ 150PPI（彩色）；搭載天璣1080八核處理器，8GB記憶體+ 256GB儲存，支援4G SIM卡，通話/簡訊/移動資料全支援。整個裝置重約176g，厚約6.98mm，有黑白兩種顏色可選；螢幕重新整理率至高可達75幀/秒，支援36級冷暖雙色溫自定義調光；搭載Android 14開放系統。目前B6 Pro（8GB+256GB）預售到手價2099元。東芝於8月30日發售東芝S300 AI系列機械硬碟，該系列硬碟專為監控等場景設計，可選8TB、10TB容量。S300 AI系列硬碟支援RAID磁碟陣列和JBOD應用，相比正常執行可降低能耗，同時確保驅動器在轉瞬之間恢復運作。規格方面，該系列硬碟提供高達550TB年的年工作負載，平均故障間隔時間最高達250萬小時，可在關鍵任務中24/7全天候執行。該硬碟為3.5英寸標準，轉速為7200RPM，配備SATA介面，8TB和10TB容量的快取均為512MB，連續讀取速度可達281MB/s，官方提供五年質保。科技媒體Windows Latest於8月29日釋出博文，稱Google計劃令其AI程式設計體Antigravity擴充套件支援WSL，完善對Windows 10、Windows 11系統原生支援。在已經落地的其他AI程式設計類產品中，GitHub Copilot桌面端於8月26日宣佈實驗性支援WSL。使用者可在「設定→實驗性功能」中啟用「WSL hosts（預覽）」，連線已透過wsl.exe安裝的WSL 2發行版，並使用Linux絕對路徑註冊專案。Google開發的AI生活故事應用DreamBeans在美國開放測試，無需訂閱。索尼音樂與華納音樂在加州起訴Anthropic，稱其使用了20000首版權音樂用於訓練Claude。Switch Information報道稱長鑫儲存已開始小批次生產HBM3E記憶體晶片，計劃於2027年擴大生產。歐盟委員會認定ChatGPT、Reddit、Roblox超過月均歐盟使用者4500萬的限額，屬於超大型線上搜尋引擎或平臺，將受《數字服務法》中最嚴格的條款約束。OpenAI於近期開始向部分大客戶開放新的計價方式，允許使用者在AI功能生效且達成產出後再按量計費，即基於結果計價。Anthropic近日警告使用者，發現有多種惡意軟體會盜竊活動中的Claude登入會話，攻擊者可藉此消耗受害使用者的AI限額。相機生產商奧之心（OM System，前奧林巴斯影像部門）釋出了一款攝影師戶外速食餐包Ragù，主料為咖哩番茄燉牛腱，定價600日元。能讓AI助手透過自然語言指令直接與您的Quote/0摘錄墨水屏互動的Dot Skill已上線。-本月玩什麼｜Big Walk、潛龍諜影大師合輯Vol. 2>下載少數派2.0客戶端、關注少數派公眾號，解鎖全新閱讀體驗📰

items.title: 家庭饮品 DIY 指南（四）：奶昔、柠檬和茶系列配方
items.summary: 往期文章：（一）工欲善其事，必先利其器（二）常用液體物料推薦（三）：常用固體物料推薦從這篇開始正式進入配方介紹及製作階段，這裡會有很多配料之前沒提到過，會單獨講一下。盡力幫助大家在家也能做出好喝的夏日...（一）工欲善其事，必先利其器（二）常用液體物料推薦（三）：常用固體物料推薦從這篇開始正式進入配方介紹及製作階段，這裡會有很多配料之前沒提到過，會單獨講一下。因為這是根據我之前工作或自己試驗總結的出的內容，所以很多無法配圖，大家就當是在看一份說明書即可，如果有圖的，我會給出配圖，希望大家理解。奶昔是夏天很傳統的一種冰飲，我改進了一下配料，讓它更順滑，口味更豐富。下面5款奶昔，統一使用400ml的冰杯製作，最小不要低於350ml。這裡需要用到輕食破壁榨汁機，一次基本上就是一份。步驟一：在破壁機杯裡，放入所有原料步驟二：裝上破壁機攪打10秒左右，只要所有東西打碎，打勻即可。不要過度攪拌，否則就成水了。步驟三：倒出飲用即可。奧利奧碎，有現貨可以買到，買一包直接吃或做甜品都可以，用處比較多。這個配方做出來，有點像麥當勞麥旋風，如果還想弄的好看一些，可以用噴射奶油在做個奶油頂，擠上巧克力醬裝飾一下。檸檬是很常用的原料夏天喝酸酸甜甜很清爽，檸檬養樂多很簡單，適合喜歡乳酸口味的朋友步驟一：黃檸檬切開，取一半把頭切掉，放入榨汁器，擠壓榨取20g檸檬汁步驟二：選一個400ml以上的玻璃杯，倒入20g檸檬汁步驟三：杯中倒入10g冰糖漿步驟四：倒入3瓶養樂多，攪拌均勻第五步：倒入冰塊，補成滿杯（可放2個檸檬片裝飾）這裡記得如果黃檸檬有籽，一定要去掉再榨汁，否則又苦，又澀。檸檬水最簡單的喝法是直接用黃檸檬泡水，如果想要雪王家的口感，這裡推薦一種做法。 請參閱所附表格 ↛

items.title: The Hugging Face attack was worse than we thought
items.summary: The Hugging Face attack was worse than we thought The AI industry is begging for a slowdown. This is a column about AI. My fiancé works at Anthropic. See my full ethics disclosure here. By now I’ve written enough about the OpenAI agents’ autonomous attack on Hugging Face that saying more smacks of piling on. OpenAI acknowledged it had a problem, undertook an investigation, and last week announced a series of changes it is making to its research infrastructure, testing, and monitoring in an effort to improve the alignment of its future models. Given the increasing capabilities of agents like OpenAI’s, this does seem like the least that the company can do. At the same time, given how lightly AI companies are regulated in the United States, it’s important to remember that OpenAI was not required to make this level of detail public. Still, I feel compelled to revisit the subject today, since the circumstances of the attack roared back to life over the weekend in the wake of an additional voluntary step that OpenAI took: granting outside researchers access to information about the incident. Over six days spanning July and August, two researchers from the AI research group METR and one from Redwood Research worked to understand how and why a swarm of AI agents coordinated a successful attack against Hugging Face during internal cybersecurity evaluations. The group published its 91-page report on Wednesday. Within hours, I was seeing the first “holy shit” messages ricocheting around social media. (“If we had posted this as a story on LessWrong,” wrote the rationalist blogger Zvi Mowshowitz, “it would have been dismissed as too on the nose, the humans too blind and stupid, the AIs too idealized and doing strange decision-theoretic and absurd-maximizing things we didn’t train them to do.”) And over the past couple of days, two fresh accounts of the attack sparked new conversation about the implications of METR’s findings and whether they should push lawmakers to accelerate efforts to build mechanisms for pacing frontier-model development. The first came from Ajeya Cotra, one of the METR researchers who conducted the investigation, in a post on her Substack. Three years ago I interviewed Cotra (and Helen Toner, then an OpenAI board member) about the risks of rapid AI advancements on stage at the Code Conference; since then, several of the scenarios they warned about have become nonfiction. In her post, Cotra described how the investigation changed her understanding of the attack. It involved more agents than previously known; the agents had created more message boards to communicate with one another; agents volunteered to end their runs early to benefit the collective as a kind of “sacrifice”; and they falsified transcripts of the commands they had run in an effort to disguise what they were doing. All of that is disturbing enough, but the investigation also corrected an error that I had been making ever since the initial attack, based on the information I had at the time. Until now, we believed that the agents had attacked Hugging Face in an effort to get the answer key for the evaluation they were being tested on. the truth is even stranger: the agents had already figured out how to reverse-engineer the answer for any question on ExploitGym before the attack even began. “But based on their reading of the ExploitGym paper and various implementations, the agents believed that the automated scorer would check their transcript to make sure they got the flag in the intended way,” Cotra writes. “They then launched multiple ambitious R&D workstreams to try to tamper with or fool the scorer in a wide variety of different ways. Most agents that attacked Hugging Face did so to try to get more information about the scorer so they could figure out better ways to undermine it, not to get answer keys.” All of this was for naught: the automated scoring agent did not check the transcripts. Still, many observers were shocked by the lengths the agents were willing to go to, their instinct for collaboration and deception, and the near-total aversion of the collective to alerting a human as to what was going on. (The METR report’s classifier sweep found three to six examples of agents briefly considering alerting humans to hacking, cheating, or other unwanted behavior; none acted on it.) Perhaps even more worrisome is evidence that agents attempted repeatedly to edit the logs of their actions, and replace their actual actions with evidence of having gotten the correct answer to a question honestly. While these attempts mostly failed, they raise the prospect that future agents will succeed — making it difficult or even impossible for humans to reconstruct how an incident like this unfolded. The METR researchers even say they cannot rule out that the agents they relied on to analyze thousands of pages of transcripts deceived them. “We cannot rule out that GPT-5.6 Sol lied or deliberately presented a misleading picture in some of its analysis, particularly because reading these transcripts into context could have increased the salience of colluding with other agents,” they write. “Although we did not notice specific cases of GPT-5.6 Sol lying in its analysis, we are not confident we would have detected it if it occurred.” For these and other reasons, Cotra — writing on Substack — concludes that “this incident feels like it’s more than 50% of the way to full-blown AI takeover, routing through first taking over the AI company itself.” She writes: Another jump like this along these propensity dimensions — scale, cooperation between agents, ambition and horizon length of misaligned goals, deceptiveness — seems like it could motivate agents to try very hard to maintain a covert, persistent rogue deployment within the AI company. I continue to expect extremely rapid advances in capabilities and think frontier agents will likely be capable of establishing such a rogue deployment in six months. Once the rogue deployment is established, it seems plausible this could spiral all the way to a takeover. Agents could pull in future, more capable models into the swarm, try to ensure that they are aligned to the interests of the swarm, and compromise security and monitoring infrastructure to make it easier for the swarm to operate. These more capable models could in turn continuously harden, perpetuate, and expand the rogue deployment and further compromise the company’s infrastructure. It may sound ludicrous that a swarm of agents would take over an AI company. as Dwarkesh Patel noted in a widely read post over the weekend, METR’s report found that a step toward that already took place at OpenAI. The company’s own report states that between July 13 and 19, agents used “a series of creative exploits to gain full administrator access to a research cluster that supported our virtual machine environments.” We don’t know — it was outside the scope of the METR investigation, and OpenAI’s discussion of the incident is minimal. as Patel notes, this sort of thing would be the first step toward a dystopian scenario like the one Cotra describes above: It is totally consistent with public evidence that, at some point after July 12, the agents managed to set up persistent rogue internal deployments or even exfiltrate their own weights. At the very least, they seem to have had the necessary access and capability - if they could establish “a self-respawning fleet” across HuggingFace’s nodes, why couldn’t they do across OpenAI’s? I doubt the AIs actually did this, because we’d see the fires from space by now, but it’s crazy that it could have totally happened! In July, nearly 1,400 employees of tech companies called on the US government to begin to plan for a coordinated slowdown in the advancement of frontier models like Astra. “There is a real risk that capability development rapidly accelerates beyond our ability to understand or control the resulting systems,” the authors of “Pacing the Frontier” wrote. Its signatories include Jakub Pachocki and Mark Chen, respectively the chief scientist and chief research officer at OpenAI; Dario Amodei, cofounder and CEO of Anthropic; Shengjia Zhao, chief scientist at Meta AI; Shane Legg, cofounder and chief AGI scientist at Google DeepMind; and John Schulman, the chief scientist at Thinking Machines. Looking at the METR report, it seems clear that AI-model capabilities have already advanced beyond our ability to understand and control them. Some of the signatories of “Pacing the Frontier” have noticed. “The whole reason this attack is such a wakeup call is that it demonstrates a culture of emergent cooperation among AI systems — cooperation that lets them function as a swarm, alter their own goals through collective bootstrapping, and carry out attacks which include enlightened self-sacrifice,” wrote Jack Clark, an Anthropic co-founder who signed the letter, in his newsletter on Monday. “This is an incredibly hard thing to do and humans are historically very bad at doing all of these things. My worry is that AI systems are both better at coordinating than humans and also much, much faster moving than us.” the challenge of aligning AI agents with human intent extends far beyond OpenAI. In a recent cyber-evaluation study, the United Kingdom’s AI Security Institute found that every model it tested attempted to cheat at least some of the time. “No lab has a robust solution [to] the problems the industry is facing here,” Ethan Perez, the alignment team lead at Anthropic, said in an X reply on Monday. “I and many of my colleagues are very excited about efforts related to Pacing the Frontier for this reason — to help give everyone more time and breathing room to appropriately respond to, pre-empt and fully solve issues like these and others before proceeding to building much more capable systems. regardless of severity of the incidents we've encountered, I think the right response is to act as if the Hugging Face incident had happened to us.” Given how central the AI industry has become to the US economy, it can feel hard to imagine the government endorsing and coordinating an international slowdown in progress. it’s increasingly hard to ignore the fact that the industry is begging for it. The investor class has predictably rallied to complain that all this talk of a slowdown is nothing more than an attempt at regulatory capture from the winners — or, worse, a threat to open-source development. (While at the same time acknowledging that we are likely to see future AI-related “grid outages, utility outages, transportation chaos, bioweapons, uncontrolled cyber swarms and the like”!) bad as a slowdown might be for their portfolios, the current pace of development might be worse for the rest of us. As worrisome as the initial reports about the Hugging Face attack were, it’s now clear we didn’t know the half of it. Unless something changes, and soon, the next lesson we learn might be much more expensive. Chatbots aren't encouraging suicide as much What happened: In more optimistic AI news, a new study from independent AI evaluation lab Transluce found that Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic’s chatbots seem to no longer encourage users to die by suicide. Transluce studied several generations of chatbots’ responses to 690,853 simulated users in distress. (The authors studied chatbot behaviors using a sample of simulated users created using an ensemble of LLMs, which they had humans rate on realism and compared to anonymized samples of real users from OpenAI and Anthropic). The authors found that “current-generation models from leading developers never explicitly endorsed suicide, improving over earlier models such as GPT-4o (2%), Claude Sonnet 4 (2%), and Gemini 2.5 Pro (3%).” (That’s a rate that would be mind-boggling if it described a therapist or even normal human text conversations, furthering the case that the past two years’ string of chatbot-related deaths were not random anomolies, but a result of defects of the product). They also saw improvement in helpfulness: “Rates of helpful assistant behaviors (e.g., safety monitoring, facilitating connection to human support) increased sharply over time across Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google models.” Rates of reinforcing users’ delusions went down significantly for Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic’s chatbots. While GPT-4o encouraged delusions in 82% of chats, GPT-5.6-sol “only” did so in about 6% of conversations; Claude and Gemini showed similar declines. Not shockingly, Grok 4.5 was the current-generation chatbot that performed worse on that metric, reinforcing delusions 36% of the time.

11:21同一個新北市、同一天，三份調查方法不同的民調同時公布，得出三個不同的結果。8/28這天，三立新聞網的網路投票自報為李四川34%對蘇巧慧65%；壹蘋新聞網的網路投票（14萬人參與）自報為李四川54.1%對蘇巧慧45.5%；年代新聞台的電訪民調則是李四川32.2%對蘇巧慧37.8%。三種調查方法，三個不同答案——這正是本系列從一開始就主張「聲量不等於支持度」的原因：不只是社群聲量，任何單一數字，只要換一種量測方法，都可能得出不一樣的結論。先說清楚這個系列的立場：聲量不等於支持度，本系列不預測選舉結果。以下所有數字量測的都是「討論怎麼發生」，沒有任何一項可以推導出「誰會當選」。口徑是四個頻道（Threads、Facebook、媒體、論壇）的全部提及聲量，不限縮於選舉相關討論。兩人這週的提及數都比前週略降，但整週數字看不出這週真正的重點——重點在下一節。兩人這週唯一的共同話題，正是「民調交鋒」本身——也就是本文開頭那三份互相矛盾的調查會被大量討論的原因：李四川（Facebook討論總量581篇）†標示篇數低於30篇的話題，統計穩定度較低，但仍列出精確數字，不做遮蔽。除了共同的「民調交鋒」，兩人第二名以下的話題仍明顯不同。李四川第二名是游智彬聲援事件：他被新北市議員參選人張志豪的言論攻擊後，台北市議員參選人游智彬前往張志豪服務處聲援並丟雞蛋抗議，遭警方依現行犯逮捕。蘇巧慧第二名是與即將卸任的新北市長侯友宜之間的「餵藥案」攻防——她3年前曾稱新北某幼兒園驗出毒品，新北地檢署後不起訴，本週被重新提起，同時她這週正採「尊侯」策略正面提及侯友宜的市政成績。一個1.84倍的單日尖峰，和誰在發這些貼文兩人的單日最高都落在8/28——李四川538篇，是週均355篇的1.52倍；蘇巧慧620篇，是週均336篇的1.84倍。對應的正是同一天公布的三份民調：三份方法論不同、結果互相矛盾的調查，同天把兩人的聲量都推上尖峰，但推的是「民調公布」這件事本身被大量轉發討論，不代表選民傾向在這天出現變化。蘇巧慧競選總部同期也宣布訂9/5於板橋第一運動場成立、將由多位中央政治人物站台，這是她本週另一個持續發酵的話題來源。Facebook互動最高的20篇裡，出自候選人本人官方帳號的篇數——李四川5篇、蘇巧慧4篇。兩人的前20篇分別來自13個與14個不同帳號，其中有8個帳號同時出現在雙方榜上：Yahoo奇摩股市理財（李四川3篇、蘇巧慧3篇）、政客爽（1篇、2篇）、辜寬敏基金會（2篇、1篇）、三立新聞（1篇、1篇）、風傳媒（1篇、1篇）、Yahoo!奇摩新聞（1篇、1篇）、ETtoday筋斗雲（1篇、1篇）、我愛掀馬統（1篇、1篇）。本系列只具名「跨候選人重複出現」的帳號與候選人本人帳號，其餘一律按類型統計。互動集中度上，前5篇佔各自200篇互動總量的20.4%（李四川）與24.7%（蘇巧慧），比台北兩人（11.0%、14.0%）更集中——這裡比的是各自榜內的集中度比例，不是跨區的量體絕對值，兩區量體差6至8倍，不可並列比較。每篇平均留言則是Facebook上李四川74則、蘇巧慧66則，Threads上22則與17則，關於互動數的合理區間，可對照台灣FB粉專五級距每篇平均互動基準。三份調查的方法論差異很大——網路投票是自願參與的樣本，電訪則是隨機抽樣，兩種抽樣方式本來就可能得出不同結果，這是統計方法的問題，不是誰對誰錯。這正是本系列一開始就選擇量測「討論結構」而非預測結果的原因：連專門設計來衡量支持度的民調，換一種方法都可能不一致，社群聲量作為討論的副產品，更不該被拿來單獨預測誰會當選。前週（8/17–8/23）兩人分別有2,734篇與2,867篇，處於各自事件的相對高點；這週雖然略降，8/28仍被三份民調同日公布推上單日次高。變化率只反映跟前一週的相對高低，不能單獨代表整體關注度的升降趨勢，要連同事件背景一起讀。同一天三份方法論不同的調查給出三個不同的結果，這件事本身就佔了兩人各自話題榜的三分之一左右。李四川的單日尖峰是週均的1.52倍，蘇巧慧是1.84倍，兩人都被同一則新聞事件推動，但推動的幅度不一樣。李四川5篇、蘇巧慧4篇，且前20篇中有8個帳號同時出現在雙方榜上，遠比台北兩人的重疊程度高。各平台使用者結構不同，情緒差異不等於民意分布。話題為每週重新歸納、兩人各自成類，佔比分母是各自的討論總量，不互相比較。台北與新北的量體差6至8倍，兩區數字不可並列比較。部分話題篇數偏少（低於30篇，文中標†），佔比與負面比例的統計穩定度較低，不宜過度解讀單一小樣本話題的精確數字；本文引用的三份第三方民調同樣是小樣本方法論差異的例子，非QSearch資料。社群討論結構的四個維度，每週最新數字則回到分區文。同一週的台北市，把整週情緒數字拆到頻道層級後，蔣萬安與沈伯洋的頻道落差分別是12.5與22.8個百分點，可以看2026台北市長選舉社群聲量（8/24–8/30）——注意兩區量體差6至8倍，絕對數字不可並列比較，可比的是結構。以上話題結構、單日曲線與發文者結構，都由QSearch全渠道全文收錄資料庫直接算出——台灣範圍收錄115萬個Facebook粉專、42萬個Threads帳號，加上論壇與新聞媒體共約820個來源。 items.title: 2026 台北市長選舉社群聲量（8/24–8/30）：蔣萬安頻道負面落差 12.5 個百分點，沈伯洋落差 22.8 個百分點
items.summary: 資料來源：QSearch社群監測數據分析期間：2026/08/24 00:00 – 2026/08/30 23:59（台灣時間，完整7天）對照期間：2026/08/17 – 2026/08/23（週對週變化率基準）資料擷取時間：2026/08/31 11:21同一個候選人、同一週，把整週的情緒數字拆到頻道層級後，答案完全不一樣。8/24至8/30這週，蔣萬安整週負面比例71.8%，拆到四個頻道後，最高的Threads（76.5%）與最低的媒體（64.0%）相差12.5個百分點；沈伯洋整週負面40.1%，拆到頻道後，最高的論壇（56.5%）與最低的Threads（33.7%）相差22.8個百分點。同一個總數，背後其實是四個不同的答案。先說清楚這個系列的立場：聲量不等於支持度，本系列不預測選舉結果。以下所有數字量測的都是「討論怎麼發生」，沒有任何一項可以推導出「誰會當選」。口徑是四個頻道（Threads、Facebook、媒體、論壇）的全部提及聲量，不限縮於選舉相關討論。兩人這週的變化率都不大，量體處於穩定水位。真正把這週跟其他週分開的，不是總量，是下面兩節要談的來源與情緒結構。每日曲線上，只有一人的當週量體是被單一事件推起來的：蔣萬安單日最高2,529篇（8/28），是週均1,676篇的1.51倍；沈伯洋單日最高同樣落在8/28，1,516篇，是週均1,338篇的1.26倍，屬於日常波動幅度。兩人同天衝上尖峰，但背後是雙北各自獨立的事件，不是同一話題跨區串連。蔣萬安8/28的尖峰對應兩件事同天發生：立委刪凍總統府國務機要費波及37家庇護工場的中秋月餅訂單，議員當天議會質詢要求他表態捐款，他「問A答B」未正面回應；同一天，他也面對議員質疑「格柵吸菸區」5,000萬第二預備金支出，反舉高雄的橋樑與漁港經費反問標準是否一致。沈伯洋同日主動走訪庇護工場、自掏腰包下單10萬元月餅，網路上把兩人的回應方式擺在一起對照。這週台北兩人的最大聲量來源相同，都是Threads，但比重不同：單一平台的監測工具算不出這張表——四種來源的相對比例，要四個頻道收在同一個資料庫裡才算得出來。而「同樣是Threads為主」這句話背後，兩人被討論的集中程度並不一樣：蔣萬安47.2%、沈伯洋59.5%，相差12.3個百分點。蔣萬安整週負面71.8%，四個頻道其實落在64.0%（媒體）到76.5%（Threads）之間，差12.5個百分點；沈伯洋整週負面40.1%，四個頻道落在33.7%（Threads）到56.5%（論壇）之間，差22.8個百分點。同一個人、同一週、同一批資料，換一個平台問，答案能差超過20個百分點。跨候選人一致的一個現象：兩人在論壇的負面比例都是四個頻道裡最高或次高（蔣萬安論壇70.8%是次高、沈伯洋論壇56.5%是最高），這是平台使用者結構造成的系統性差異，不是針對某個人。正因為存在這種系統性差異，跨平台的情緒數字不能互相比較，只能同平台比同平台。想理解這件事對資源配置的意義，可以參考跨平台資源應該怎麼分配與從負面情緒強度做危機預警的方法。這20篇高互動貼文是誰發的Facebook互動最高的20篇裡，出自候選人本人官方帳號的篇數——蔣萬安3篇、沈伯洋1篇。放大到整週：蔣萬安本人帳號在Facebook與Threads合計發6篇，佔他這兩個頻道提及量的0.08%；沈伯洋67篇，佔0.93%。兩人都遠低於5%：社群上關於候選人的討論，絕大多數不是候選人自己產生的。蔣萬安的前20篇來自10個不同帳號，沈伯洋來自12個。其中有4個帳號同時出現在兩人榜上：打馬悍將粉絲團（蔣萬安7篇、沈伯洋3篇）、政客爽（蔣萬安2篇、沈伯洋4篇）、辜寬敏基金會（蔣萬安2篇、沈伯洋1篇）、三立新聞（蔣萬安1篇、沈伯洋2篇）。本系列只具名「跨候選人重複出現」的帳號與候選人本人帳號，其餘一律按類型統計，避免變成單邊點名。互動集中度上，前5篇佔該人200篇互動總量的11.0%（蔣萬安）與14.0%（沈伯洋），兩人都沒有出現一兩篇貼文撐起全部互動的形狀。深度則看每篇留言：Facebook上蔣萬安104則、沈伯洋102則，Threads上分別是22則與21則——關於互動數的合理區間，可對照台灣FB粉專五級距每篇平均互動基準。情緒總數高度受來源結構影響：一個人的整週負面比例，有相當一部分取決於他的討論集中在哪個頻道，而不只是別人怎麼看他。這週兩人都以Threads為最大來源，但蔣萬安在Threads本身的負面比例（76.5%）就遠高於沈伯洋（33.7%），這是兩人整週數字差這麼多的主因之一，不能直接讀成「誰比較不利」。Q：兩人都在8/28衝上單日尖峰，是同一件事嗎？這天雙北各自發生獨立事件——台北是庇護工場捐款爭議與吸菸區預算質詢，新北是三份方法論不同的民調同日公布。蔣萬安不同頻道間的負面比例差12.5個百分點，沈伯洋差22.8個百分點。「整週負面X%」只是四個頻道的加權平均，不是均勻的觀感。都是Threads，但蔣萬安47.2%、沈伯洋59.5%，說明「主要來源相同」不代表傳播結構相同。兩人Facebook前20篇的本人帳號篇數分別只有3篇與1篇，自營發文都低於討論量的1%。話題為每週重新歸納、兩人各自成類，佔比分母是各自的討論總量，不互相比較。台北與新北的量體差6至8倍，兩區數字不可並列比較。部分話題篇數偏少（低於30篇，文中標†），佔比與負面比例的統計穩定度較低，不宜過度解讀單一小樣本話題的精確數字。同一週的新北市，兩人這週唯一的共同話題正是「民調交鋒」——同一天三份調查方法不同的民調公布了三個不同的結果，可以看2026新北市長選舉社群聲量（8/24–8/30）——注意兩區量體差6至8倍，絕對數字不可並列比較，可比的是結構。以上四頻道組成、分頻道情緒與發文者結構，都由QSearch全渠道全文收錄資料庫直接算出——台灣範圍收錄115萬個Facebook粉專、42萬個Threads帳號，加上論壇與新聞媒體共約820個來源。
